title: Research Integrity Investigations Administrator
description:
Under the direction of the Research Integrity Officer, the Grant Compliance Administrator I provides substantive administrative, analytical, and investigative support for the University’s research-integrity and research-misconduct program. The position supports the full lifecycle of matters involving alleged fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, and related research-integrity concerns, from the initial receipt and documentation of allegations through preliminary assessment, inquiry, investigation, institutional decision-making, required reporting, corrective-action monitoring, and case closeout. The position also assists in distinguishing matters that fall within the University’s research-misconduct process from authorship disputes, honest error, differences of scientific opinion, general research noncompliance, employment concerns, and other issues that may require referral to a different institutional office or process.

The position manages sensitive and frequently complex case records; monitors procedural requirements, deadlines, and required notifications; and supports the preservation, sequestration, organization, and review of research records and other potentially relevant evidence. Responsibilities include assisting with structured interviews; reviewing publications, research data, laboratory and electronic records, correspondence, policies, and other documentation; developing factual chronologies; identifying evidentiary consistencies, discrepancies, and gaps; and preparing accurate, neutral, and well-supported summaries, memoranda, notices, correspondence, and draft reports.

The Grant Compliance Administrator I coordinates the administrative activities of inquiry and investigation panels, including conflict-of-interest screening, scheduling, preparation and secure distribution of case materials, meeting support, documentation of procedural actions, and tracking of panel requests and deliverables. The position also facilitates appropriate coordination among the Research Integrity Officer, University counsel, information technology, colleges, faculty and academic leaders, research administrators, sponsors, collaborating institutions, journals, and governmental oversight agencies. The position exercises independent judgment and applies research-integrity subject-matter expertise when analyzing assigned matters, identifying procedural or evidentiary risks, determining necessary follow-up, and recommending appropriate next steps. All work must be performed impartially and with strict attention to confidentiality, evidence integrity, procedural fairness, recordkeeping, and applicable University, sponsor, and governmental requirements. The position does not independently make final findings of research misconduct or other institutional determinations; those authorities remain with the Research Integrity Officer, review panels, and other officials designated by University policy.

The University of South Florida is a top-ranked research university serving approximately 50,000 students from across the globe at campuses in Tampa, St. Petersburg and USF Health. In 2025, U.S. News & World Report recognized USF with its highest overall ranking in university history, as a top 50 public university for the seventh consecutive year and as one of the top 15 best values among all public universities in the nation. U.S. News also ranks the USF Health Morsani College of Medicine in the highest tier, placing it as one of the top 16 medical schools in the nation and inside the top 10 among public universities. USF is a member of the Association of American Universities (AAU), a group that includes only the top 3% of universities in the U.S. With an all-time high of $750 million in research funding in 2025 and as a top 20 public university for producing U.S. patents, USF uses innovation to transform lives and shape a better future. The university generates an annual economic impact of nearly $10 billion for the state of Florida. USF’s Division I athletics teams compete in the American Conference. Learn more at .

The primary duties and responsibilities for this position include:
• Receives and documents allegations and related information; supports initial triage and preliminary assessments of jurisdiction, applicable definitions, specificity, credibility, time limitations, and other threshold considerations.
• Coordinates evidence-preservation and sequestration activities with the Research Integrity Officer, University counsel, information technology, colleges, and other offices; maintains organized records of collection, custody, access, and disposition.
• Conducts or supports structured, neutral interviews; reviews research records, publications, electronic communications, policies, and other evidence; develops chronologies and identifies material consistencies, inconsistencies, gaps, and follow-up needs without prejudging outcomes.
• Administers inquiry and investigation panels, including conflict-of-interest screening, appointment and scheduling support, preparation of case materials, meeting coordination, deadline tracking, and documentation of procedural actions.
• Drafts notices, correspondence, case summaries, procedural memoranda, interview summaries, reports, and other written materials for review by the Research Integrity Officer, panels, University counsel, and designated institutional officials.
• Maintains secure and confidential case files, case-management records, status reports, and audit trails; monitors procedural deadlines, required notifications, corrective actions, and matter closeout in accordance with applicable requirements.
• Coordinates, as directed, with respondents, complainants, witnesses, faculty and academic leaders, research administrators, sponsors, collaborating institutions, governmental oversight agencies, and other stakeholders while preserving appropriate role boundaries and confidentiality.
• Researches and analyzes applicable laws, regulations, sponsor requirements, institutional policies, and procedural standards; assists with development of procedures, templates, training materials, and process improvements that support consistent and defensible case administration.
• Identifies and promptly escalates conflicts of interest, threats to evidence, procedural risks, public health or safety concerns, sponsor-reporting issues, retaliation concerns, and other matters requiring institutional action.

title: AI and Data Literacy Lead
description:
Make your mark for patients

Artificial Intelligence and Data Capability Lead

We are looking for an Artificial Intelligence and Data Capability Lead who is practical, collaborative, and outcome-oriented to join our Transformation team, named Ruby, based in the United States or in Europe : Either in our headquarters in Belgium or in UK, Slough.

About the role

You will build the practical artificial intelligence and data literacy that enables teams to use data and emerging technologies confidently, responsibly, and effectively in their daily work. You will translate expectations into role-specific learning, practical guidance, and supported application within real business workflows. This business-facing role focuses on helping people understand, evaluate, and use data and artificial intelligence in practice. You will also challenge teams to rethink how their processes can evolve, while ensuring appropriate human judgment, verification, and measurable business value.

Who you’ll work with

You will be working in a team that operates across the Patient Evidence organisation, within Data Products Operations. You will collaborate with business leaders, portfolio and product leads, business analysts, subject matter experts, data and technology teams, and partners in learning, change, communications, privacy, and compliance. Together, you will connect learning to priority business questions, available data products, and technology-enabled capabilities, while building confidence and encouraging responsible, evidence-based use.

What you’ll do

  • Define and maintain an artificial intelligence and data literacy framework aligned with business roles, decisions, and workflows.
  • Assess capability needs, identify priority audiences, and address learning gaps and barriers to adoption.
  • Translate complex data, analytics, governance, and artificial intelligence concepts into clear, practical business language.
  • Design role-based learning paths, playbooks, examples, working sessions, and reusable learning resources.
  • Embed learning into real business questions, data products, and technology-enabled workflows.
  • Build understanding of data meaning, origin, quality, limitations, and suitability for purpose.
  • Promote responsible use through human oversight, output verification, and evidence-based decision-making.
  • Measure proficiency, application, confidence, adoption, and business impact, using feedback to continuously improve learning.

Interested? For this role we’re looking for the following education, experience and skills

  • A bachelor’s degree in data, analytics, artificial intelligence, business, learning, organisational development, life sciences, or a related field. An advanced degree or relevant professional qualification is preferred.
  • Experience in data, analytics, digital transformation, learning, change, or business enablement roles.
  • Experience translating complex data and artificial intelligence concepts into practical guidance for non-technical audiences.
  • Experience designing role-based learning, capability frameworks, learning resources, and applied learning experiences.
  • Experience supporting adoption and behaviour change within a complex, collaborative organisation.
  • Understanding of data quality, governance, semantics, analytics, and responsible artificial intelligence principles.
  • Strong facilitation, communication, coaching, and storytelling skills, with the ability to connect learning to measurable outcomes.
  • Experience in pharmaceuticals, healthcare, or life sciences is preferred.

Are you ready to ‘go beyond’ to create value and make your mark for patients? If this sounds like you, then we would love to hear from you!

About us
UCB is a global biopharmaceutical company, focusing on neurology and immunology. We are over 9.000 people in all four corners of the globe, inspired by patients and driven by science.

Why work with us?
At UCB, we don’t just complete tasks, we create value. We aren’t afraid to push forward, collaborate, and innovate to make our mark for patients. We have a caring, supportive culture where everyone feels included, respected, and has equal opportunities to do their best work. At UCB, we’ve embraced a hybrid-first approach to work, bringing teams together in local hubs to foster collaborative curiosity. Unless expressly stated in the description or precluded by the nature of the position, roles are hybrid with 40% of your time spent in the office.

UCB is an equal opportunity employer. All employment decisions will be made without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable laws.

title: Coach
description:
The Coach is responsible for coaching clients over virtual meetings and calls to help them improve their sales skills using the NEPQ methodology. The Coach will be accountable for delivering high-quality coaching and training that helps clients achieve their goals and improve their performance using this methodology. In addition, the Coach is expected to assist in sales and support for live and virtual events.

Essential Job Functions

  1. Client Needs Discovery:

    • Conduct discovery calls with clients, documenting their needs and developing an action plan over the course of their program to help them achieve their goals using NEPQ methodology.

  2. 1:1 Client Coaching:

    • Build a strong relationship with clients that encourages transparency and trust.

    • Schedule and lead 1:1 coaching calls with clients according to action plan.

    • Document client progress and achievements for each coaching session.

    • Provide coaching on a wide range of sales skills including prospecting, presentations, negotiation, closing, and account management using the NEPQ methodology.

    • Assess client progress and give regular feedback for improvement.

  3. Group Coaching:

    • Plan, schedule, and lead group coaching calls, keeping the discourse on topic and professional.

    • Plan and lead group role-play activities.

    • Document summary of group session and outcomes.

  4. Personal Development:

    • Stay up-to-date on all NEPQ and 7th Level materials and processes, completing new modules as they are released.

    • Continuously monitor industry trends in coaching and commit to remaining current.

    • Provide regular reports to leadership on client feedback, successes, and struggles, as well as suggestions for improvement to the program.

  5. Perform other miscellaneous functions and special projects as assigned.

Performance Measurements

  1. Client Needs Discovery:

    • Every client has a documented needs-analysis and action plan that is properly maintained and stored in agreed-upon accessible locations.

  2. 1:1 Client Coaching:

    • Client feedback on your sessions are overwhelmingly positive.

    • Meet the minimum KPIS for calls completed, quality of sessions, and length of sessions.

    • Coaching calls with clients happen on schedule and follow the action plan.Client progress and achievements for each coaching session are documented and stored in agreed-upon accessible location.

    • Coaching plans address clients needs in prospecting, presentations, negotiation, closing, and account management using the NEPQ methodology as appropriate.

    • Client progress and regular feedback for improvement is provided to the client.

  3. Group Coaching:

    • Group coaching calls occur according to schedule and receive favorable feedback from the clients.

    • Group role-play activities are relevant to the group and provide positive outcomes.

    • Group sessions and outcomes are documented and stored in agreed-upon accessible location.

  4. Personal Development:

    • Up-to-date on all NEPQ and 7th Level materials and processes, and modules, ensuring that all coaching sessions are only using what is current.

    • Continuously monitor industry trends in coaching and commit to remaining current.

    • Provide regular reports to leadership on client feedback, successes, and struggles, as well as suggestions for improvement to the program.

Qualifications

Education/Certification:

Bachelor’s degree in Business Development, Education, or related field preferred, but equivalent experience plus high-school diploma will also be considered.

Required Experience:

Minimum 2 years experience in Sales, Business Development, or online coaching or other relevant experience.

Strong track record of providing excellent customer service.

Required Skills/Abilities:

Exceptional communication and relationship management skills, especially in high-stakes, revenue-driven environments.

High proficiency in project management.

Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities

Excellent organizational and time management skills

Proficient in Google Suite

Proficient in data analysis

Excellent creative thinking and problem-solving skills.

Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise discretion

Ability to multitask and prioritize

Strong attention to detail

Travel:

  • Movements frequently and regularly required using the wrists, hands, or fingers.

  • Sedentary work; sitting most of the time. Exerts up to 25 lbs. Of force occasionally.

title: Foam Application Technician
description:
Essential Responsibilities FIP Machine Operation & Process Control
  • Set up, operate, and monitor FIP gasket equipment used to apply gasket material to doors, side panels, and other components.
  • Operate the machine's PLC and control system, including selecting, creating, modifying, and saving jobs for various parts.
  • Verify proper machine setup, job selection, material settings, and operating parameters prior to beginning production.
  • Monitor machine operation and make appropriate adjustments to maintain consistent gasket placement and product quality.
  • Understand machine set points and recognize abnormal operating conditions that could affect equipment, production, or product quality.
  • Minimize material waste, downtime, equipment damage, and nonconforming products through proper process control.
Troubleshooting & Equipment Maintenance
  • Identify and troubleshoot machine faults, alarms, error codes, and process issues.
  • Perform routine cleaning and basic maintenance of the FIP system, including the application nozzle and associated equipment.
  • Understand the three-component chemical system used by the FIP equipment and recognize conditions that may affect material flow, application, or gasket quality.
  • Communicate equipment issues that cannot be resolved at the operator level to Maintenance or appropriate supervisory personnel.
Quality, Blueprint Reading & Measurement
  • Read and interpret blueprints, technical drawings, work orders, and product specifications.
  • Verify proper gasket placement, dimensions, measurements, and finished-product quality.
  • Use calipers and other measuring equipment accurately.
  • Apply strong math and measurement skills to ensure products meet established specifications.
  • Identify and communicate quality concerns or nonconforming conditions.
Material Management
  • Monitor FIP chemical and material levels to ensure adequate supplies are available for scheduled production.
  • Recognize material conditions that could negatively affect machine performance or finished-product quality.
  • Communicate replenishment needs and material concerns before they impact production.
Assembly & Production Support
  • Safely and effectively use hand tools and other equipment required for machine setup, adjustments, minor maintenance, assembly, and production activities.
  • Assist with assembly and other production activities as needed to support departmental and plant requirements.
  • Maintain awareness of production priorities and upcoming jobs to ensure required components are completed on schedule.
  • Review work orders, production information, and schedules to anticipate upcoming requirements and prioritize work accordingly.
Shipping & Material Coordination
  • Prepare completed products and materials for shipment.
  • Complete required billing and shipping documentation.
  • Verify shipment quantities and ensure the correct number of parts, skids, and components are prepared for each shipment.
  • Locate jobs, work orders, components, and materials throughout the facility and determine their status when information is not readily available.
  • Maintain awareness of incoming and outgoing truck schedules and shipping priorities.
  • Coordinate loading, paperwork, shipment information, and other shipping requirements with truck drivers and internal personnel.
  • Identify and resolve discrepancies involving work orders, quantities, material locations, and shipment requirements.
Communication & Cross-Functional Coordination
  • Communicate effectively with Production, Shipping, Maintenance, Supervision, and other departments.
  • Proactively identify upcoming production or shipping needs that could affect schedules.
  • Maintain sufficient knowledge of related production and shipping processes to provide support when needed.
  • Assist with or provide basic training to employees on FIP machine operation, shipping procedures, work order identification, and other responsibilities within the scope of the position.
Required Qualifications
  • Ability to read and interpret blueprints, technical drawings, work orders, and specifications.
  • Strong mathematical and measurement skills.
  • Ability to properly use calipers and other measuring equipment.
  • Ability to operate and navigate PLC and machine-control systems.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude with the ability to troubleshoot equipment and process issues.
  • Ability to safely and effectively use hand tools.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to product quality.
  • Strong organizational, communication, and time-management skills.
  • Ability to independently locate information, work orders, parts, and materials.
  • Ability to effectively coordinate with multiple departments and manage changing priorities.
Physical Requirements
  • Ability to frequently lift and handle materials weighing up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods throughout the workday.
  • Ability to bend, reach, push, pull, grasp, and safely handle parts, materials, tools, and equipment.
  • Ability to safely perform work associated with FIP operations, assembly, production, and shipping.
Safety & Compliance
  • Follow all company safety policies, procedures, and established work practices.
  • Properly use all required personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hearing protection, safety footwear, gloves, and additional PPE required when working with FIP chemicals or equipment.
  • Follow established procedures for the safe handling, use, and storage of chemicals associated with the FIP process.
  • Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work area.
  • Report unsafe conditions, equipment concerns, and potential hazards to the appropriate personnel.
Key Competencies
  • Mechanical Aptitude
  • Technical Problem Solving
  • Attention to Detail
  • Quality Focus
  • Organization & Time Management
  • Communication
  • Production Coordination
  • Shipping Coordination
  • Independent Decision-Making
  • Adaptability & Prioritization

title: JSOC Operator ll
description:
Are you interested in joining an organization with a global reach? In a world of shifting threats, Concentric is your trusted ally. Powered by elite professionals from military, government, and intelligence backgrounds. If you are passionate about intelligence, risk analysis, threat management, executive protection, security operations, or business resiliency, Concentric may be the organization you’ve been searching for!

Concentric is a risk consultancy specializing in delivering strategic security and intelligence services. We provide holistic, intelligent security solutions for private clients and corporations globally. Concentric offers strategic advisory services, risk assessments, physical protection, threat intelligence, open-source monitoring, program audits, secure embedded staffing, and training for security teams and intelligence analysts.

Our ultimate goal is to be recognized as the most innovative, capable, and trusted Risk Management partner in the world, and we do this by following these core values:

Integrity – Collaboration - Relationships – Excellence – Creativity - Results

Join Us,

Concentric - "Your World Secured"

We are currently hiring a JSOC Operator ll to join our team embedded with our client in Redwood City, CA!

JOB DESCRIPTION

This position requires the Operator to use intelligence sources, internal and external assets, and open-source media to identify threats and provide timely and accurate information to company leadership. The Operator will identify and monitor viable hazards to employees, operations, global assets, and the brand, reporting these threats to the company’s leadership team, 24/7.

The JSOC Operator will use a set of emergency response procedures to manage critical incidents, provide clear assessment and reporting of the situation, and determine appropriate actions to resolve the incident. The threats and critical incidents that the Operator needs to track, disseminate, and manage include political instability, violence, travel alerts, health concerns, man-made or natural disasters, internal threats or technical failures. The JSOC Operator may also be tasked with assisting investigators by researching and compiling open-source information.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Conduct continuous collection and review of open source information utilizing multiple systems and sources to detect potential threats.
  • Manage, coordinate, and disseminate crisis management information and directives during declared emergencies and/or preventative actions mitigating potential emergencies.
  • Act as a focal point for all threat-related information using all appropriate and available communications and systems.
  • Actively monitor travel safety and security of employees on a global, 24/7 basis.
  • Assist various internal teams by performing initial collection of intelligence points as requested.
  • Liaise closely with key partners to ensure purpose and scope of responsibilities in threat mitigation.
  • Identify threats and assist team members with providing a resolution of security incidents through analysis, investigations and prioritization of incidents based on risk/exposure.
  • Assist the operations team with travel booking and scheduling, particularly during non-regular business hours.
  • Be the first point of contact for incoming calls, clients, deliveries and requests to the Company and assist with administrative tasks when needed.
  • Work closely with Residential Security Teams to track daily incidents and roving patrol activity, and monitor camera systems across assigned properties.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in criminal justice, international security, political science, or a related field.
  • Military service or prior experience working in a JSOC, GSOC or similar operations center may be substituted for educational requirements.
  • This position requires up to <5% travel.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Preferred 2 years of demonstrated experience doing the following:
    • Effective assessment and evaluation of sensitive situations
    • Quickly and accurately identify and respond to critical issues
    • Research, investigate, compile, and assess information
    • Demonstrate planning and organizational skills
    • Skilled in synthesizing facts, concepts, and principles

title: Lead Data Engineer - Data Platform
description:
Overview

This is a remote role that may be hired in several markets across the United States. Priority given to those candidates located in North Carolina, Arizona, Texas and Florida.

We are seeking an experienced Lead Data Engineer to join our Data Platform Engineering Organization and lead the design, development, and modernization of enterprise data platforms that power analytics, reporting, business intelligence, and operational decision-making across the organization.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on data engineering leader with expertise in cloud-based data platforms, data warehousing, ETL/ELT development, and modern data engineering practices. This individual will be responsible for delivering scalable data solutions utilizing AWS Services, Snowflake, dbt, Python, SQL, and related technologies while mentoring team members and driving engineering excellence.

As part of our growing Cloud Data and AI Platform organization, you will lead and collaborate with a talented team of engineers, product partners, and business stakeholders to deliver enterprise data products and cloud-based data solutions. This role offers the opportunity to mentor engineering talent, drive engineering best practices, and support the adoption of modern data engineering capabilities across the organization.


Responsibilities & Qualifications

Duties and Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will have experience working in large enterprise environments and partnering with cross-functional teams to deliver trusted data products that support strategic business objectives.

  • Lead the design, development, and implementation of enterprise data solutions utilizing AWS Services, Snowflake, dbt, Python, SQL, and related cloud technologies.
  • Develop and support data warehouses, Operational Data Stores (ODS), and ETL/ELT pipelines that enable analytics, reporting, and operational data capabilities.
  • Design and implement batch and real-time data processing solutions using modern streaming and event-driven architectures.
  • Partner with business stakeholders, analysts, and technology teams to translate business requirements into scalable data solutions.
  • Define and promote data quality strategies, testing standards, governance practices, and compliance controls across the data platform lifecycle.
  • Establish enterprise testing practices, including data validation frameworks, dbt testing standards, and quality controls to support trusted data products.
  • Define monitoring, observability, and operational reliability standards, including dashboards, alerts, service-level objectives (SLOs), and service-level agreements (SLAs) for enterprise data platforms.
  • Establish deployment strategies, environment promotion standards, and release governance practices that support secure and reliable delivery across enterprise data platforms.
  • Contribute to technical discussions, peer reviews, and knowledge-sharing initiatives across the data engineering team.
  • Leverage AI-powered development and productivity tools to accelerate solution delivery, improve code quality, and enhance engineering productivity

Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree and 6 years of experience in Data Engineering, Data Warehousing, Cloud Data Platforms, or related technology disciplines.

OR

High School Diploma or GED and 10 years of experience in the same areas.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Advanced experience with modern data warehousing and large-scale data processing technologies such as Snowflake, Spark, or equivalent platforms.
  • Advanced proficiency in Python and SQL.
  • Advanced experience designing, developing, orchestrating, and supporting ETL/ELT pipelines and data integration solutions using tools such as dbt, Apache Airflow, Astronomer, or equivalent cloud-native data engineering technologies.
  • Advanced experience with data modeling, data warehousing, and data engineering best practices.
  • Experience designing, developing, and supporting scalable, reliable, and high-performing data engineering solutions in enterprise environments.
  • Experience collaborating with business and technology stakeholders to deliver data-driven solutions.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

Following qualifications are a plus

  • Advanced experience with enterprise ETL/ELT tools such as DataStage, SAP BODS, SSIS, Informatica, or equivalent technologies.
  • Experience developing and supporting Operational Data Stores (ODS), analytics platforms, and data products.
  • Experience with Snowflake Cortex, Change Data Capture (CDC), streaming, and real-time data ingestion technologies including Kafka, Amazon Kinesis, Qlik Replicate, Snow pipe Streaming, or equivalent platforms.
  • Experience integrating data across AWS, on-premises, and Snowflake environments, with exposure to enterprise security, governance, and compliance frameworks.
  • Experience with Data Vault modeling and modern data warehousing methodologies.
  • Experience leading technical initiatives, mentoring team members, and promoting engineering best practices.
  • Experience within Financial Services, Banking, or other highly regulated industries.
  • Familiarity with Tableau, Power BI, or other analytics and visualization platforms.
  • Experience using AI-powered development and productivity tools to improve engineering efficiency and delivery outcomes.
  • AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate, AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate or Professional, SnowPro Core Certification, SnowPro Advanced Data Engineer Certification, or equivalent cloud and data platform certifications.

Additional Information

This job posting is expected to remain active for 45 days from the initial posting date listed above. If it is necessary to extend this deadline, the posting will remain active as appropriate. Job postings may come down early due to business need or a high volume of applicants.

If hired in North Carolina, the base pay for this position is generally between $128,935 and $168,000. Actual starting base pay will be determined based on skills, experience, location, and other non-discriminatory factors permitted by law. description:
Silicon Ranch is a fully integrated provider of customized renewable energy, carbon, and battery storage solutions for a diverse set of partners across North America.

  • We are known for putting community partnerships first, and are the only renewable energy company in the U.S. that owns and operates all of its solar ranches and has a 100% track record for successful delivery.

  • We have the largest utility scale agrivoltaics portfolio in the country under Regenerative Energy®, our nationally recognized holistic approach to project design, construction, and land management. Our model incorporates regenerative ranching and other regenerative land management practices to restore livelihoods and soil health, biodiversity, and water quality.

  • Through our subsidiary, Clearloop, we are able to help businesses of all sizes reclaim their carbon footprint with a direct investment in building new solar projects while also helping bring renewable energy and economic development to distressed communities.

By joining Silicon Ranch, you will be joining a team of experienced and dedicated individuals who have proven time and again that it is indeed possible to not only “make solar do more”, but to make the promise of carbon-free, renewable energy that benefits people right where it comes from a tangible, measurable, and replicable reality.

Silicon Ranch is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace that is reflective of the communities in which we work and serve. We are an equal opportunity employer and will consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other legally protected characteristics.

Job Description

Position: Solar PV Operations and Maintenance Area Lead III - Field Operations (Georgia sites)

Location: Various GA sites (Hazlehurst, Jesup, Vidalia, Waycross, and Douglas)

Overview:

This position is responsible for the performance and leading of corrective and preventative maintenance tasks within a defined set of facilities. These tasks include the inspection, troubleshooting, diagnosis, and remedy of issues impacting the production of the solar PV facility. This includes repair and/or replacement of electrical and mechanical components and subcomponents such as contactors, breakers, motors, bearings, PV modules, PLCs, transformers, etc, as well as the troubleshooting of complex electrical systems.


The ideal candidate is a self-starter with a strong mechanical inclination and verifiable experience performing in a utility scale operations and maintenance role. Experience performing and leading maintenance tasks on DC, AC, and MV systems, communications equipment, and mechanical systems will translate well to this position.

PV solar operations and maintenance experience is required to be considered for this role. Candidates must have direct on-site management experience at NERC-regulated facilities with a capacity of 100 MW or greater.

Main Responsibilities

● Perform and lead scheduled preventive maintenance tasks at each facility, including the full PV system, UPS, SCADA, substation, and MV/HV/OHE systems.

● Perform and lead corrective maintenance tasks, both scheduled and unscheduled, at each facility, including the full PV system, UPS, SCADA, substation, and MV/HV/OHE systems.

● Respond to directives for emergency dispatches for critical systems as directed.

● Log all work performed via the Silicon Ranch CMMS platform.

● Perform electrical testing using IV Curve Tracers, Power Quality Meters, Insulation Resistance Testers, Multimeters, and other testing equipment as needed.

● Assist management with field investigations to support predictive analytics, root cause analysis, and serial defect reports.

● Assist in creating and reviewing preventative and corrective maintenance SOP’s, schedules, and checklists.

title: Partnerships & Development Associate
description:
About The Engine

As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit and public benefit organization, The Engine supports Tough Tech founders working to solve the world's most pressing challenges in climate, health, and advanced systems. We do this through powerful founder programs and resources, access to shared infrastructure and labs, and by convening a national network of philanthropic, corporate, and government partners, investors, universities, experts, and other organizations committed to helping breakthrough technologies reach the world.

The Engine's community includes approximately 160+ companies developing science- and engineering-based technologies across areas including energy, advanced materials, biotechnology, manufacturing, computing, robotics, and other advanced systems.

About the Role

The Engine is seeking a Partnerships & Philanthropy Associate for a full-time position providing direct support to the Director of Partnerships and the Director of Philanthropy in prospecting, executing, and managing strategic partnerships and philanthropic relationships across our Tough Tech ecosystem.

Reporting to the Director of Partnerships and the Director of Philanthropy, this role will work closely with philanthropic, corporate, and ecosystem partners, founders, and internal teams to translate relationships advancing The Engine’s impact and mission, and creating tangible opportunities for The Engine's community of Tough Tech founders and strengthening the ecosystem.

The Associate will work closely with the Directors of Partnerships and Philanthropy to identify and execute philanthropic and industry partnership opportunities, steward existing relationships, and facilitate connections between founders and industry partners, funders, and resource providers that help companies develop and scale breakthrough technologies more efficiently.

This is a highly collaborative and execution-oriented role for someone who is interested in managing philanthropic and industry engagements that scale Tough Tech.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage partner engagement and stewardship - Execute partner meetings, workshops, Ignition Pass programs, Innovation Days, founder programming, and philanthropic stewardship, including matching partners with relevant Engine companies, managing relationships with foundation, corporate, and individual funders, tracking grant requirements and reporting deadlines, and drafting funder updates, grant reports, and related stewardship materials.

  • Run operations and CRM - Track funder and partner commitments, deliverables, and follow-ups in the CRM and keep records current. Coordinate invoicing and payment follow-up with Finance. Support pipeline and revenue forecasting.

  • Conduct research and prospecting - Build prospect profiles and research lists for Directors to review. Research philanthropic organizations, companies, industries, technologies, and funders to find partnership opportunities that fit The Engine's mission.

  • Support and coordinate events - Plan logistics for philanthropic and strategic events. Coordinate vendors and venues, manage invite lists and RSVPs, and staff events on-site.

  • Prepare collateral, materials, and deliverables - Build company shortlists, briefing documents, presentations, meeting materials, partner updates, funder reports, and follow-up emails.

  • Support special projects - Contribute to ecosystem initiatives and other projects as needed.

Qualifications

We recognize that strong candidates may come from a variety of academic and professional backgrounds. The ideal candidate will bring a combination of technical curiosity, business judgment, relationship-building skills, and strong execution.

  • 2–3 years of relevant professional experience in partnerships, business development, philanthropy, nonprofit development, program management, or a related field.

  • Bachelor's degree required. An advanced degree in a relevant technical or business field may substitute for up to two years of professional experience.

  • Strong interest in philanthropy, emerging technologies, entrepreneurship, commercialization, corporate innovation, or the startup ecosystem.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage projects, coordinate multiple stakeholders, and deliver against commitments and deadlines.

  • Ability to quickly understand complex scientific or technical concepts and communicate their commercial relevance to nontechnical audiences.

  • Strong interpersonal skills and comfort engaging with founders, funders, corporate executives, technical experts, and other external stakeholders.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare professional correspondence, presentations, and briefing materials.

  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple projects, relationships, and follow-up activities simultaneously.

  • Demonstrated initiative, sound judgment, and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment.

  • Strong research, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

  • Comfortable working both independently and collaboratively across teams.

Preferred Experience

Experience in one or more of the following areas is preferred:

  • Philanthropy, fundraising, grant management, or nonprofit development

  • Startups, accelerators, incubators, or entrepreneurship programs

  • Corporate innovation, strategy, business development, or partnerships

  • Technology commercialization or university technology transfer

  • Consulting or other analytically rigorous business environments

  • Scientific or engineering research

  • Climate tech, biotech, advanced manufacturing, robotics, computing, materials, or other Tough Tech sectors

  • Event planning, program coordination, or project management

  • CRM platforms and relationship-management tools

Location: Dublin, Ireland or London, England

Summary/Overview:

KBRA’s Regulatory and Government Affairs team is seeking a highly motivated Director to support the firm’s engagement with regulators, policymakers, and industry stakeholders across the UK and Europe. This position offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of financial regulation, capital markets, and public policy while contributing to KBRA’s regulatory and government affairs initiatives.

This role will serve as KBRA’s primary Regulatory and Government Affairs representative based in Europe, helping to expand the firm’s regulatory profile and strengthen relationships with policymakers and supervisors throughout the region. The Director will support ongoing engagement with UK and EU regulators, national competent authorities, policymakers, public officials, trade associations, and other industry stakeholders on issues affecting credit rating agencies and the broader financial services industries.

The Director will monitor policy and regulatory developments, conduct policy research and analysis, prepare materials for senior leadership, coordinate regulatory outreach, and support strategic engagement across Europe. This role is ideal for candidates with experience in European financial regulation, public policy, government affairs, or regulatory engagement who are looking to take on significant responsibility in a collaborative and fast-paced environment.

About the Job:

Regulatory and Policy Monitoring

  • Monitor and analyze policy, regulatory, and supervisory developments affecting credit rating agencies and the broader financial services sector across the United Kingdom and the European Union.
  • Track emerging regulatory initiatives from the European Commission, European Parliament, ESMA, EBA, EIOPA, ECB, FCA, BOE, HMT, and national competent authorities.
  • Assess the potential implications of regulatory developments for KBRA and the credit markets.

Policy Research and Analysis

  • Conduct research and prepare analyses on key European and UK policy initiatives related to capital markets, securitization, banking regulation, insurance regulation, sustainable finance, artificial intelligence, digital finance, operational resilience, and oversight of credit rating agencies.
  • Prepare briefing memoranda, policy summaries, consultation analyses, executive briefings, speeches, and talking points for senior management.

Regulatory and Government Engagement

  • Develop and maintain productive relationships with European and UK regulators, policymakers, public officials, supervisory authorities, trade associations, and industry participants.
  • Represent KBRA in meetings with regulators and policymakers throughout Europe.
  • Coordinate and support responses to public consultations, policy proposals, and regulatory initiatives.
  • Help strengthen KBRA's visibility and reputation through ongoing engagement with key stakeholders across Europe.
  • Participate in industry conferences, regulatory roundtables, consultations, and policy forums throughout the UK and Europe.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with Legal, Compliance, Communications, Business Development, and Analytical teams to support coordinated regulatory strategy and consistent external messaging.
  • Provide regulatory intelligence and policy guidance to business leaders across the organization.
  • Coordinate European regulatory initiatives with KBRA's Regulatory and Government Affairs teams across the globe.

Special Projects

  • Contribute to strategic initiatives related to regulatory developments, public policy priorities, and industry trends.
  • Assist with projects involving regulatory coordination and external engagement efforts.

About You:

  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred in Public Policy, Political Science, Economics, Law, International Relations, Finance, or a related field.
  • Approximately 6–10 years of experience in financial regulation, government affairs, public policy, legislative affairs, or a related field.
  • Strong understanding of financial regulatory and policy processes.
  • Excellent research, writing, analytical, and communication skills, with the ability to distill complex policy issues clearly and accurately.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects independently while collaborating effectively across teams.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail in a fast-paced professional environment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite; familiarity with policy tracking tools, regulatory databases, or financial market research platforms is a plus.
  • Familiarity with Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT for research, data insights, and productivity enhancement is a plus.

What You Will Gain

  • Direct engagement with many of the world's leading financial regulatory institutions.
  • Opportunities to influence regulatory discussions affecting global capital markets.
  • Experience working directly with senior leadership on international regulatory strategy.
  • Exposure to cross-border financial regulation and policy development.
  • Opportunities to travel throughout Europe and build relationships with policymakers, regulators, and industry leaders.
  • A collaborative, mission-driven culture that values independence, integrity, and analytical excellence.
  • A hybrid working environment based in London or Dublin with significant opportunities for international engagement.

Benefits

  • A flexible hybrid work schedule – Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays in the office
  • Competitive benefits and paid time off
  • Paid family and disability leave
  • Pension plan
  • Educational and professional development financial assistance
  • Employee referral bonus program

About Us

KBRA (Kroll Bond Rating Agency, LLC) is a full-service credit rating agency registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission as an NRSRO. Kroll Bond Rating Agency Europe Limited is registered as a CRA with the European Securities and Markets Authority. Kroll Bond Rating Agency UK Limited is registered as a CRA with the UK Financial Conduct Authority pursuant to the Temporary Registration Regime. In addition, KBRA is designated as a designated rating organization by the Ontario Securities Commission for issuers of asset-backed securities to file a short form prospectus or shelf prospectus. KBRA is also recognized by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners as a Credit Rating Provider. Kroll Bond Rating Agency Europe is located at 2nd Floor, One George's Quay Plaza, George's Quay, Dublin 2 D02 E440. Kroll Bond Rating Agency UK is located at 1st Floor, Marble Arch House, 66 Seymour Street, London W1H 5BT, England.

title: Windows Systems Engineer
description:
Requisition Id 17240

**Active DOE Q, active DOD Top Secret, or active DOD TS/SCI clearance is required for consideration.**

**­­Overview:**

We are seeking a Windows Systems Engineer who will play a crucial role in managing and supporting Windows servers and large storage systems! Areas of focus include maintaining system health, analyzing system performance, and ensuring all activities are documented in accordance with National Security Sciences and customer requirements. This position resides in the Support Services & Isolated Environments group in the Research Computing division of the Information Technology Services Directorate at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL).

This team supports the ORNL’s goals through robust systems engineering, integration, and support tailored specifically for our NSS research community. We manage a variety of critical infrastructures including mid-range clusters, servers, workstations, and other pivotal services.

**Major Duties/Responsibilities:**

**Systems Administration:**

- Manage, configure, and maintain Windows server environments, including Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS, and DHCP.
- Monitor and optimize system performance, ensuring uptime and reliability.
- Perform regular system updates, patches, and backups.
- STIG checking and systems compliance.

**Virtualization & Storage:**

- Implement and support VMware virtualized environments tailored for Windows systems.
- Manage storage solutions relevant to Windows environments, ensuring data integrity and availability.

**Security & Compliance:**

- Implement and maintain security best practices for Windows systems.
- Ensure compliance with organizational policies and standards.

**Customer Service & Support:**

- Provide advanced support and troubleshooting for Windows-based systems.
- Collaborate with stakeholders to resolve technical issues and provide recommendations for system improvements.
- Deliver high-quality customer service, both internally and externally.

**Project Management & Documentation:**

- Lead or participate in projects related to Windows infrastructure, from design to implementation.
- Create and maintain comprehensive documentation for all system configurations, processes, and procedures.
- Prioritize and manage multiple tasks and projects efficiently.
- Update and maintain all documentation as required.
- Deliver ORNL’s mission by aligning behaviors, priorities, and interactions with our core values of Impact, Integrity, Teamwork, Safety, and Service. Promote equal opportunity by fostering a respectful workplace – in how we treat one another, work together, and measure success.
- Other duties as assigned or required.

**Basic Qualifications:**

- A BS in information technology, information systems, computer science, computer engineering, business, science, or a related field of study and a minimum of five years of Windows systems engineering and administration experience is required for consideration. An overall combination of equivalent education and experience may be considered.
- Active DOE Q, active DOD Top Secret, or active DOD TS/SCI clearance is required for consideration.

- Proven expertise in managing Windows server environments, including Active Directory, DNS, and other core services.
- Strong knowledge of virtualization technology.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

- Experience working at a DOE facility
- Familiarity with NSS federal computer systems and compliance standards is a plus.
- Experience with scripting and automation (e.g., PowerShell).
- Experience with STIG hardening.
- Knowledge of network infrastructure as it relates to Windows environments.
- Experience in SANs: preferred experience with EqualLogic, EMC, Synology, NetApp is desired.
- Experience with building and managing a Citrix and VMware virtualization platforms.
- Experience with Thin Clients is desired.
- Experience with Wyse Management Suite is desired.
- Familiarity with COMSEC.
- Experience with BigFix.

- Excellent written and oral communication skills.
- Motivated self-starter with the ability to work independently and to participate creatively in collaborative teams across the laboratory.
- Ability to function well in a fast-paced research environment, set priorities to accomplish multiple tasks within deadlines, and adapt to ever changing needs.

**Special Requirements:**

- Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
- This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a clearance from the Department of Energy. As such, this position is a Workplace Substance Abuse (WSAP) testing designated position. WSAP positions require passing a pre-placement drug test and participation in an ongoing random drug testing program.

**About ORNL:**

As a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Science national laboratory, ORNL has an impressive 80-year legacy of addressing the nation’s most pressing challenges. Our team is made up of over 7,000 dedicated and innovative individuals! Our goal is to create an environment where a variety of perspectives and backgrounds are valued, ensuring ORNL is known as a top choice for employment. These principles are essential for supporting our broader mission to drive scientific breakthroughs and translate them into solutions for energy, environmental, and security challenges facing the nation.

ORNL offers competitive pay and benefits programs to attract and retain individuals who demonstrate exceptional work behaviors. The laboratory provides a range of employee benefits, including medical and retirement plans and flexible work hours, to support the well-being of you and your family. Employee amenities such as on-site fitness, banking, and cafeteria facilities are also available for added convenience.

Other benefits include the following: Prescription Drug Plan, Dental Plan, Vision Plan, 401(k) Retirement Plan, Contributory Pension Plan, Life Insurance, Disability Benefits, Generous Vacation and Holidays, Parental Leave, Legal Insurance with Identity Theft Protection, Employee Assistance Plan, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, Wellness Programs, Educational Assistance, Relocation Assistance, and Employee Discounts.

This position will remain open for a minimum of 5 days after which it will close when a qualified candidate is identified and/or hired.

We accept Word (.doc, .docx), Adobe (unsecured .pdf), Rich Text Format (.rtf), and HTML (.htm, .html) up to 5MB in size. Resumes from third party vendors will not be accepted; these resumes will be deleted and the candidates submitted will not be considered for employment.

If you have trouble applying for a position, please email ORNLRecruiting@ornl.gov.

ORNL is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants, including individuals with disabilities and protected veterans, are encouraged to apply.  UT-Battelle is an E-Verify employer.

title: Specialist, Contract Management Pharmaceutical Development
description:
Purpose

The Contract Management Specialist is responsible for the timely and appropriate execution of Confidentiality Disclosure Agreements (CDAs), Clinical Study Agreements (CSAs), associated Budgets, and vendor agreements, the legal sections of the Informed Consents and issues on other legal, compliance, regulatory and policy matters (such as Insurance Policies, FMV, FCPA, etc.). In partnership with Legal they ensure that issues and points of negotiation are settled rapidly in support of our new model to minimize or eliminate negotiation and our aspirational target of first pass acceptance of these documents. The overall aim is to keep CDAs, Contracts and Budgets off the clinical study critical path for all AbbVie studies (both Site Management & Monitoring and CRO conducted studies). The responsibility is Global – all countries except US, Puerto Rico and Japan.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the point person for their country/region for Legal, Finance, Site Management & Monitoring and Study Team.
  • Accountable for the timely preparation and execution of CDAs, CSAs and Budgets and related vendor agreements, either directly or via local staff where a region is supported and language requires local help. Budgets should be in line with Country Fair Market Value (FMV) and actuals should be monitored. Deviations from legally approved contract templates should be approved by Legal and should be in line with guidance provided by Legal.
  • Direct negotiation of CDAs, CSAs and Budgets with investigator sites using templates, guidance and playbook from Legal where language is not a problem, or with the help of the monitor where local language necessitates. Deviations from legally approved contract templates should be approved by Legal and should be in line with guidance provided by Legal.
  • Input into legal aspects of the Informed Consents to ensure first pass acceptance or rapid resolution of issues using the Legal playbook/guidance or Legal consult if necessary.
  • Liaising with Legal where playbook doesn’t already address an issue and seeking Legal approval for deviations.
  • Setting, managing and communicating priorities to local affiliate stakeholders, Legal, and Finance in alignment with study plans and priority for start-up.
  • Provide input into ongoing update of the playbooks and templates with Legal.
  • Tracking CDAs and CSAs in the appropriate systems and collecting relevant metrics.
  • Collecting and tracking site intelligence and communicating such to appropriate stakeholders in the Study Team, Legal, Finance, etc.
  • Ensuring that CDAs and CSAs are off the critical path for study start-up or study continued conduct where change orders are needed mid-study – meeting timeline commitments.
  • Appropriate tertiary qualification, health related (Medical, Scientific, Nursing) preferred.
  • Minimum three years clinical research experience including contract/budget negotiation. Proven negotiating skills, tact and diplomacy.
  • Understanding of medical and legal terminology and the application of business/financial concepts used in clinical research.
  • Extensive knowledge related to ICH/GCP guidelines and applicable local regulations.
  • Ability to learn multiple concepts related to legal, compliance and regulatory matters in clinical research.
  • Good planning and organizational skills and the ability to work effectively and efficiently in a dynamic environment with competing projects and deadlines.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities/projects.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills. Written and verbal fluency in English and local language (if not English).
  • Strong sense of urgency and ability to make decisions.
  • Good communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Positive team player.
  • Good observational skills, analytical and conceptual capabilities.
  • High degree of flexibility when facing changes in the work environment.

description:
NEOTech is a leading provider of manufacturing technology and supply chain solutions for brand name OEMs in the industrial, medical and military/aerospace markets. The company's headquarters is based in Chatsworth, CA with additional locations in the U.S. and Mexico.

Summary

The Program Manager (PM) is the “voice of the customer (VOC)” and leader of the Customer Focus Team (CFT). The PM is accountable for the operational performance to the customer and the achievement of NEOTech’s internal financial performance of the customer. The PM works directly with Account Management (AM) and site General Manager (GM) to drive business growth organically and/or with Business Development (BDM) to launch new customers.   • Lead CFT meetings and maintain notes/action items shared internally and with the customer. Follows-up internally to close NEOTech’s action items with appropriate team members and works closely with the customer to ensure customer’s action items are closed and support where needed
  • Leads weekly/monthly meetings with customers (frequency depends on customer)
  • Responsible for sales order process as it relates to customer change requirements.
  • Drive customer satisfaction while ensuring NEOTech’s best interests/goals/financials are achieved
  • Manages internal communication of metrics (inventory turns, quality, delivery (OTD), tariffs / duty recovery, PPV’s, E&O, etc.) as well as metrics with the customer (monthly or quarterly depending on the customer)
  • Communicates NCNR parts to customers and had the customer signoff. Give date and if no signature then escalate to Account Manager if no response from customer. Do not place parts order if signature is not received

  • ECO/ECN implementation and present cost impact to the customer with recovery PO
  • Work closely with Operations to ensure timely implementation of production schedules.
  • Ability to interface with key managers at NEOTech to achieve escalation of projects as required for completion
  • Support and follow all ISO standards related to NEOTech’s various Quality Management Systems, and all corporate and site 5S objectives.
  • Present excess & obsolete (E&O) to customer on a monthly basis and drive resolution, work with AM for resolution. Coordinate the program Excess & Obsolete (E&O) Mitigation Plan.

title: Java Backend Developer
description:
De ICT afdeling, team Victorie bij Beeld & Geluid, houdt toezicht op de volledige IT-infrastructuur. Dit varieert van het interactieve museum tot een state-of-the-art media assetmanagement- en archiveringssysteem dat alle content van de Nederlandse publieke omroepen duurzaam bewaart en beschikbaar stelt. Ook de digitalisering straat, met high-end filmscanning- en editing apparatuur, valt onder onze verantwoordelijkheid.

Locatie: Hilversum
Uren: 40 uur per week
Salaris: € 4.445,53 - € 6.350,65

Wat ga je doen?

Als Java Backend Developer, speel je een cruciale rol in het ontwerpen, ontwikkelen en implementeren van backend-oplossingen voor onze applicaties. Je bent niet alleen medeverantwoordelijk voor het schrijven van hoogwaardige code, maar ook voor het optimaliseren van de infrastructuur en het stroomlijnen van het ontwikkelproces.

Wie zijn wij?

Wij zijn in de eerste plaats een van de grootste en meest vooruitstrevende media-archieven ter wereld. We bewaren diverse soorten media, zoals radio- en televisieprogramma’s, video(games), geschreven pers, politieke prenten, podcasts, websites en objecten. Als betrouwbaar media-instituut bewaren we onze dagelijks groeiende mediacollectie als erfgoed voor de eeuwigheid en brengen we deze collectie tot leven.

Met zo’n 500 bevlogen collega’s, waarin we onze zeer waardevolle vrijwilligers en stagiairs natuurlijk meetellen, dragen we iedere dag vanuit ons veelkleurige pand in Hilversum bij aan een open, vrije, inclusieve en mediawijze samenleving.

Wie ben je?

  • Je hebt minstens 5 jaar aantoonbare ervaring met Java 17, Spring (Boot), Hibernate, Elasticsearch, SQL, IntelliJ IDEA, TDD;
  • Je bent aantoonbaar in staat om vanaf scratch een oplossing voor uiteenlopende problemen te ontwerpen;
  • Je bent geïnteresseerd in DevOps-methodologieën;
  • We vinden het een grote pre wanneer je Scrum ervaring hebt;
  • Je bent bekend met cloudplatforms zoals (AWS/Azure/) en containerisatie (Docker, Kubernetes);
  • Je beschikt over een groot probleemoplossend vermogen en je hebt aandacht voor details bij het schrijven van code en het implementeren van oplossingen;
  • Je hebt uitstekende communicatieve vaardigheden en je bent een teamspeler;

Ons aanbod

Je eerste contract is een jaarcontract. Als we blij zijn met elkaar verlengen we met veel plezier, tot het einde van het project. Het bruto maandsalaris (op fulltime basis) is minimaal € 4.445,43 en maximaal € 6.350,65 (schaal 11 CAO Beeld & Geluid).

Hoe leuk werken bij Beeld & Geluid ook is, we hechten ook veel waarde aan vrije tijd. Per jaar heb je daarom maar liefst 25 vakantiedagen en 24 atv-dagen (op fulltime basis). Krijg je die niet op? Dan kun je ook je vakantiedagen inzetten voor andere leuke dingen, zoals de aanschaf van een (elektrische) fiets, laptop of het verwezenlijken van een droomreis. Hiervoor maken we gebruik van een cafetariamodel.

Wij geloven dat de échte magie op de werkvloer ontstaat: dáár gebeurt het! Daarom ontmoeten we elkaar graag op kantoor en is het uitgangspunt dat je minimaal 50% van je tijd op kantoor werkt. Natuurlijk kijken we altijd met een schuin oog naar de dynamiek van je functie en je persoonlijke omstandigheden: maatwerk is altijd bespreekbaar, net zoals een vaste thuiswerkdag per week. Je ontvangt een onkostenvergoeding voor thuiswerken en voor woon-werkverkeer, afhankelijk vanuit waar je werkt!

Deze vacature staat gelijktijdig intern en extern uit. We kiezen voor de meest passende kandidaat, bij gelijke geschiktheid heeft de interne kandidaat voorrang.

description:

This role supports U.S. Department of Defense customers. Employees may be assigned to different projects over time, including projects involving defense operations.

At Mile 2, applications are reviewed by real people—not filtered out by bots. Authenticity matters more than keyword tricks.

We know you're probably using AI tools to help draft or polish your resumes, and that’s fine! We're using AI to write this blurb about AI! But we expect you to make it your own. We do this by utilizing a multidisciplinary, human-machine systems approach to eliminate operational friction and context-switching bottlenecks.   • Project Leadership and Technical Oversight: Serves as Principal Investigators or lead engineers on multi-disciplinary projects, driving technical execution, research integrity, and strategic alignment with defense stakeholders.
  • Actionable Recommendations and Reporting: Delivers comprehensive CSE systems reports and actionable recommendations to enhance situational awareness, mitigate cognitive overload, and improve decision-making timeliness in high-stakes operational environments.

title: Payment Analyst
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Payment Analyst based in Switzerland.

Join a newly established Payment Operations team focused on creating end-to-end visibility across a complex payment funnel serving millions of active users.
You’ll investigate payment performance across more than a dozen payment service providers, identifying issues before they become business-critical.
Your analysis will help distinguish technical defects from user-behavior patterns and uncover the bottlenecks with the greatest impact on authorization and conversion.
You’ll turn complex payment and customer data into clear insights that can guide Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Fraud teams.
The role offers significant autonomy, with the opportunity to build diagnostic processes, dashboards, alerts, and reporting capabilities from the ground up.
You’ll work in a fast-moving environment where experimentation, practical problem-solving, and small proof-of-concepts are preferred over lengthy planning cycles.
This is an opportunity to become a trusted expert on payment funnel health while directly contributing to measurable improvements in a rapidly scaling international business.

Accountabilities

  • Take diagnostic ownership of checkout and payment funnel health, proactively identifying alerts, anomalies, insights, and defects before they become business-critical.

  • Lead root-cause investigations into funnel drop-offs and payment declines, distinguishing technical or engineering issues from user-behavior patterns.

  • Analyze authorization rates, decline codes, payment performance, and other funnel metrics to identify the highest-impact bottlenecks and improvement opportunities.

  • Investigate performance across multiple payment service providers and identify differences, outages, or recurring issues requiring attention.

  • Support regular funnel reporting for cross-functional stakeholders, translating payment data into clear insights and recommendations that can improve authorization rates and conversion.

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Fraud teams to investigate payment issues, processor outages, and other funnel-related challenges.

  • Communicate technical and analytical findings clearly to stakeholders who may not have deep payments expertise.

  • Build and improve dashboards, alerts, reporting, and diagnostic processes that increase visibility into payment funnel performance.

  • Develop into a trusted point of contact for payment funnel health, helping establish best practices within the broader team.

  • Work proactively in an evolving environment, creating practical solutions from first principles where established processes or playbooks do not yet exist.

    • Requirements:

    • Hands-on understanding of payment funnels and payment operations, including concepts such as interchange, decline codes, foreign exchange (FX), tokenization, 3DS, and fraud fundamentals.

    • Demonstrated experience performing root-cause analysis on funnel drop-offs, declines, or payment performance issues, including distinguishing technical causes from behavioral patterns.

    • Ability to analyze complex data and customer-behavior insights and communicate findings clearly to audiences without extensive technical or payments expertise.

    • Strong investigative mindset, with the initiative to independently identify and explore issues rather than waiting for predefined tasks.

    • Comfortable working in ambiguous, fast-changing environments where processes and playbooks may still be developing.

    • Nice to have: Familiarity with self-service BI and dashboarding tools to accelerate independent analysis.

    • Nice to have: Strong SQL skills for conducting independent investigations and data analysis.

    • Nice to have: Experience working in a high-growth or rapidly evolving organization.

    • Nice to have: Experience comparing payment performance across multiple PSPs.

    • Strong English communication skills, as English is the primary working language in the international team.

      • Benefits:

      • Competitive salary: €40,000–€60,000 per year, with compensation potentially varying according to experience and seniority.

      • Employee stock options: Opportunity to participate in an employee stock options program.

      • Performance incentives: Access to various bonus programs, including performance-based and referral bonuses.

      • Additional paid leave: Opportunities to earn additional paid time off through applicable bonus programs.

      • Learning budget: Personal budget dedicated to professional development and learning.

      • Paid volunteering: Opportunities to participate in volunteering activities during paid working time.

      • Flexible work location: Choose between office-based and remote work, with opportunities to combine work and travel.

      • International environment: Work in a global team where English is the primary business language.

      • Career development: Strong opportunities for personal and professional growth supported by structured feedback and promotion processes.

      • High-impact role: Help scale a fast-growing international marketplace while directly contributing to payment performance, customer conversion, and business growth.

      • Autonomy and ownership: Join a newly formed function where you can help establish processes, tools, and ways of working from the ground up.

title: Software Engineer
description:
About Us 🚀

At Immutable, our mission is to drive the next evolution of gaming. One of the hardest part of gaming is finding the players it deserves. Thousands of games launch every month, most never reach the audience they've already earned. That's the problem Immutable exists to solve, and it's why we built Audience, our growth platform for game studios. We're growing faster than we ever have, and we're hiring the talent who'll take it further. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Sydney, Australia.

A bit about the role 🤔

Immutable is looking for a hands-on product engineer to build Audience, the MarTech platform that decides whether a game succeeds. This role sits at the intersection of engineering, product, and data and you'll own outcomes, not just tasks.

The work spans multiple initiatives including attribution and measurement (built from scratch, so studios can see which marketing actually drives players), engagement (a lifecycle and messaging engine built for games), AI growth (an AI CMO that audits a studio's marketing and recommends the next best action) and more.

You'll Be Empowered To (responsibilities) 🎮

  • Own features end to end, from the customer problem through to shipping into a live product used by paying game studios
  • Build attribution and measurement such as, click tracking, identity capture, install attribution, and conversion postbacks that work natively
  • Shape Engage, our lifecycle and messaging engine across campaigns, journeys, segmentation, deliverability, and A/B testing
  • Help build our AI CMO, and the orchestration layer that lets it beat a generic model by encoding real marketing expertise
  • Work AI-native by default, using Cursor, Claude Code, and our own coding agents in the pull-request loop
  • Work directly with Product, Design, Data, and our founders, and talk to the studios using what you build.

You may be a good fit if you 🤝:

  • 4+ years of engineering experience in a product-driven environment
  • Energised in an ambiguous environment
  • Strong hands-on experience with TypeScript (both frontend and backend) and Golang is a must have
  • Empathy-driven communication and the ability to work across varied stakeholders
  • Experience mentoring and sharing best practices with junior engineers
  • Passion for user-first product development and operational excellence
  • Start-up or Entrepreneurial experience is a plus
  • Keen interest in Gaming and a willingness to learn fast

Strong candidates may also have experience with:
  • Have built product at a marketing, growth, attribution, customer-data, or customer-engagement company, and terms like segments, attribution, user acquisition, CDP, CEP, lifecycle, and deliverability are second nature
  • Have taken a product from 0 to 1, defining the first version and cutting scope yourself, and you think customer-problem-first
  • Build with AI agents day to day, and have real opinions about where they help, where they don't, and when not to trust them
  • Building and shipping AI or LLM-powered product features

Our Stack: TypeScript, Go, Next.js and React, a BigQuery-based customer data platform, AWS and GCP, Kubernetes, and AI tooling including Cursor and Claude Code. We track our work in Linear.

How we work: Small teams that own their outcomes. Fast iteration on CI/CD rather than big-bang releases. AI does the mechanical work so you can focus on judgement, taste and the customer.

We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every qualification above. The strongest candidates often bring an unexpected background, and we'd rather hear from you than have you rule yourself out. We build for a global community of players, and we want a team that reflects it.

We are proud of the benefits that we offer for all of our employees globally.

Here is a snapshot 😊

Attracting the best global talent
💸 We commit to paying globally competitive base salaries and contributions to a long-term fund

📊 Sharing our products' success through Employee Stock Options ESOP

🌟 Our flexible working model blends the best of both worlds: Sydney-based employees enjoy hybrid 3 days a week in our vibrant head office, while remote team members can work from home or utilise access to global office hubs via a WeWork All-Access pass

🥘 Lunch is ordered fresh every day in our friendly office in Sydney CBD

🎉 Quarterly End of Cycle Celebration Awards

💻 USD $500 WFH allowance to set up your home office

☎️ USD $600 per annum to put toward your internet and phone usage.

🥳 USD $75 per quarter for remote employees to celebrate with local team members

⛑️ We also support our US Employees with Medical and 401K Insurance

🚘 Our Australian Employees can access Novated Leasing and save money by paying fort their car using pre & post-tax dollars

Levelling up your growth

🌱 We offer up to USD $1,350 per annum for classes, courses, AI tooling or events to support your growth and development

📚 Enjoy access to free online courses via Udemy

Helping you thrive

💆🏽‍♀️ Enjoy USD $800 per year to put toward your health and wellbeing

🤗 Get 24/7 access to unlimited counselling for you and your family when you need it through our EAP Service

🎁 Monthly subsidy and discounted rate with ClassPass, including a 1-year free membership to Breethe

Leave when you need it the most:

👨‍👧‍👦 Paid parental leave

🌟 Enjoy 2 additional paid annual leave days at the end of the year

🎂 Enjoy a paid day off on your birthday

Additional Information:

Immutable is committed to building and fostering an inclusive, diverse workplace. We believe in incorporating everyone's perspectives and experiences as this has been a significant driver of our success so far.

We are a 2026 Circle Back Initiative Employer. This means a human reviews every application and we commit to responding to every applicant.

*A note to recruitment agencies: Our internal team has this role covered, so there is no need to reach out - We don't accept unsolicited agency resumes and are not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes. Thank you!

Join us in shaping the future of gaming!
