title: Deputy Fire Marshal
description:
General Description


Join a mission-driven team dedicated “To Prevent and Protect From Harm” as our next Deputy Fire Marshal at the City of Albany.

The Albany Fire department seeks to fill a two-year limited duration federally grant funded position. Although the City is actively working towards long term funding to extend the assignment, continued funding is not guaranteed. This position is not eligible to participate in State conflagration deployments while under grant funding.

The Deputy Fire Marshal is responsible for promoting community safety through code enforcement, fire investigation, and risk reduction through technical expertise and authority in interpreting and applying fire and building regulations. The role ensures compliance with City ordinances and State fire codes, supports safe development and occupancy of buildings, and contributes to citywide preparedness and resilience. Work is performed with independence and requires strong judgment, collaboration with internal departments and external agencies, and the ability to communicate complex regulatory requirements to diverse audiences.


**Applications will be reviewed as received and this recruitment may close at any time after October 20 without prior notice**

Completion of the application process includes the following requirements. Each of the following must be submitted prior to being considered.
  • Submit an online application on City's website: City of Albany Application
  • Submit the following certifications with your application:
    • ICC Fire Inspector I
    • NFPA Fire Inspector I
    • OSFM Fire & Life Safety Competency Recognition at the level of Fire Inspector I

Salary & Specialty Incentives:
  • Spanish or American Sign Language Incentive: $123.05 semi-monthly; $2,953.28 annually
  • Longevity Incentive:
    • 3% at 10 years of service
    • 6% at 15 years of service
    • 9% at 20 years of service

Benefits include:
  • Full medical, vision and dental coverage for employee and all eligible dependents with City paying approximately 95% of premium. Currently, the employee-paid premium is $74.38 per semi-monthly pay period for employee-only and family coverage.
  • 5 hours of vacation leave per semi-monthly pay period, with progressive increases
  • 4 hours of sick leave per semi-monthly pay period
  • 10 holidays per calendar year
  • Excellent retirement benefits:
    • City-paid participation in the Oregon Public Employee Retirement System (OPSRP and IAP)
    • City-paid contribution of 2.5% into pre-tax deferred compensation plan
  • In addition, other benefits such as education reimbursement, employee assistance program, basic life insurance, long-term disability, and flexible spending accounts for healthcare and childcare expenses.

Essential Functions/Duties & Responsibilities


The following duties represent the primary responsibilities of the position and are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed. This list is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or assignments that may be required. Employees may be assigned additional duties that are similar, related to, or a logical assignment for the classification.

  1. Conducts fire and life safety code compliance inspections on properties and inside structures of all occupancy types identified in the Oregon Fire Code; legacy fire/building codes; City ordinances; state and local laws; and any codes, regulations, or standards referenced in those codes. Requires alteration of structures, equipment, manufacturing processes, fire protection systems, roadways, use or storage of materials, site characteristics, and construction methods to meet regulations.
  2. Visits premises of new construction and existing buildings under improvement to assist in the enforcement of Oregon Fire Code and referenced codes related to fire and life safety. Provides inspection-related comments to the Building Official or their designee concerning provisions of the Oregon Fire Code. Contacts owners, developers, and contractors concerning fire apparatus access and water supply provisions of the Oregon Fire Code; assists in explaining code deficiencies and in providing alternative solutions that meet the intent of the Oregon Fire Code.
  3. Witnesses and supports the Building Department with acceptance tests of fire protection equipment such as fire alarm fire sprinkler, hood suppression and other similar protection features.
  4. Participates in Public Education events such as school programs, conducting safety talks to care facilities, installation of smoke and CO alarms in residences.
  5. Participates in the Fire Department’s Investigation Group and may be assigned as Group Coordinator; investigates fires to determine the area of origin and cause; and completes all necessary documentation. Gathers information at fire investigations by such techniques as interviewing victims and witnesses, as well as through analysis of physical evidence and other related factors in order to determine area of origin and cause. . Handles confidential information concerning fire-related criminal activity in coordination with law enforcement agency criminal investigations.
  6. Testifies as a witness regarding fire prevention and fire investigations, in both civil and criminal court actions.
  7. Reviews and follows up on third-party inspection reports on fire protection and life safety systems installed on premises and within buildings. Follows up with building and business owners concerning system impairments and code-required system repairs; explains the impact of impairments; and obtains code compliance.
  8. Receives, answers, and acts upon concerns and complaints from the public and coworkers.
  9. Establishes and maintains records relevant to the position; maintains files and a filing system; and submits information as needed for Division and Department reports.
  10. Prepares and presents clear, concise, and effective oral and written reports to architects, contractors, developers, citizens, and property owners on City ordinances, the Oregon Fire Code, and other fire and life safety regulations.
  11. May respond to fire and other emergencies to operate within the Incident Command System as an Investigation Group Supervisor or other assigned position.
  12. Exercises independent judgment in determining actions to be taken regarding fire and life safety matters within position assignment duties.
  13. Participates in drills and training necessary to maintain skills as determined by the Fire and Life Safety Division Chief.
  14. Provides input in the formulation of Division and Department goals and objectives and for the preparation of the Fire & Life Safety Division annual budget.
  15. May access Protected Health Information (PHI) and other patient information only to the extent that it is necessary to complete job duties.
  16. Expected to protect the privacy of all patient information in accordance with Department privacy policies, procedures, and practices as required by federal and state law, and in accordance with general principles of professionalism as a healthcare provider.
  17. Expected to report, without the threat of retaliation, any concerns regarding Department policies and procedures on patient privacy and any observed practices in violation of those policies to the designated Privacy Officer.
  18. Represents the Fire Department effectively on employee, City, county, and state committees and at meetings of commercial/residential development and fire code compliance.
  19. Represents the City of Albany by responding to the public, citizens, its employees, and others in a prompt, professional, and courteous manner while continuously maintaining a positive customer service demeanor. Regards everyone, internal and external, as a customer and deliver the best service possible in a respectful and patient manner.
  20. Serves as a member of various City committees as assigned.
  21. Assists other staff in the performance of their duties as assigned.
  22. Fosters a cohesive work environment by building and maintaining respectful, professional relationships with colleagues, leadership, elected officials, and members of the public.
  23. Maintains regular job attendance and adherence to working hours.
  24. Operates a motor vehicle safely and legally.
  25. May provide training and orientation to newly assigned personnel.
  26. Performs other related duties as required/assigned.

Organizational Responsibilities

Employees are expected to contribute to the effective operation of the City by providing high-quality service; supporting a culture of collaboration, accountability, professionalism, and continuous improvement; and demonstrating leadership from any seat through taking ownership of one’s work, demonstrating initiative, identifying opportunities for improvement, contributing solutions, supporting colleagues, and acting in alignment with the City’s Mission, Vision, Values, and organizational priorities regardless of position or title.

Employees are responsible for complying with applicable laws, regulations, City policies, procedures, and ethical standards; appropriately protecting confidential, private, and sensitive information while supporting the City’s commitment to transparency and public accountability; exercising sound judgment; using City resources, equipment, technology, and information responsibly, safely, and efficiently; maintaining regular and reliable attendance and arriving prepared and on time for work, meetings, training, and other work-related functions; demonstrating professional conduct and appearance consistent with City expectations and the requirements of the position; operating vehicles, when applicable to the position, safely and responsibly and in accordance with applicable laws, policies, and procedures; following reasonable direction and completing assigned work in accordance with established expectations and deadlines; adapting to changing priorities; supporting organizational initiatives; and contributing to a respectful and inclusive work environment.


Supervision/Lead Work Exercised


Reporting Relationships

Reports to: Division Chief – Fire Marshal

Review of Work/ Supervision Received: Receives general direction from the supervisor. Works independently within established policies, procedures, and expectations and exercises judgment in planning, prioritizing, and completing assignments. Guidance is provided on significant issues, changing priorities, or matters involving broader organizational impact.

Supervision Exercised: This is a non-supervisory position. Employees in this position do not have responsibility for supervising or directing the work of other employees. May provide assistance, information, training, or technical guidance to others related to assigned duties or areas of expertise.

Qualifications & Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

The qualifications described below are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Equivalent combinations of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, licenses, and certifications that provide the required competencies may be considered, unless otherwise required by policy, regulation, or law.

Education and Experience

A Deputy Fire Marshal must possess an equivalent combination of experience or training that provides the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the essential functions of the job.

Graduation from high school or possession of GED and one year’s work experience in fire prevention, fire investigation, building architecture or construction; or two years of paid structural fire suppression work; or an associate degree from an accredited college in Code Inspection, Fire Prevention/Insurance Risk, Fire Science, Fire Prevention of Building Technology, or a related field.

Licenses and Certifications

Possession of the following certifications is required: ICC Fire Inspector I, NFPA Fire Inspector I, OSFM Fire & Life Safety Competency Recognition at the level of Fire Inspector I or greater or the ability to achieve recognition within a year. Youth Fire Setter Intervention Specialist certification is preferred.

Ability to obtain the following certifications by the end of probationary period: ICC Fire Inspector II, NFPA Fire Inspector II, NFPA Instructor I, OSFM Fire & Life Safety Competency Recognition at the level of Fire Inspector II, and be working towards NFPA Fire Investigator.

By end of probationary period: National Incident Management System ICS- 100, 200, 700, 800, AWR-160. 1.

Possession of or ability to obtain a valid Oregon driver's license and a driving record that meets the City's driving record standards.

Additional Requirements

Use of cigarettes is prohibited, and the use of any tobacco product is prohibited while involved in City of Albany events.

Must successfully pass a thorough background investigation, medical and psychological exams, and drug screen prior to employment.

The individual shall not pose a direct threat to the health or safety of the individual or others in the workplace.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Knowledge of: fire prevention laws, ordinances, rules and regulations; the fundamentals of fire suppression, fire prevention, and fire origin/cause investigations; building construction and building, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical systems as they relate to fire code compliance and fire investigations; fire protection systems and modern techniques and practices in fire protection; and mechanical, chemical, and related characteristics of a wide variety of flammable, explosive, and similar hazardous materials within 24 months of the date of hire.

Skill in: operation and use of general tools and equipment previously listed and specialized items such as self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA), camera, small tools, and other specialized equipment used while conducting fire origin and cause investigations.

Ability to: locate, diagnose, and define existing and potential hazardous conditions in buildings and installed processes; make recommendations leading to the enforcement of appropriate laws and ordinances with firmness, tact, and impartiality; and communicate effectively, verbally and in writing; understand and carry out written and oral instructions; establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees, other departments, and the public even in confrontational and other difficult situations; operate computers for data entry.


Working Conditions

The work environment, physical demands, and equipment and technology described below are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

Work Environment

In the performance of the job duties, the employee will regularly work in outside weather conditions and may work in nighttime weather, congested traffic, and unsafe road conditions. The employee will occasionally work near moving mechanical parts and explosives, and in high, precarious places. They will occasionally be exposed to wet and/or humid conditions, fumes or airborne particles, toxic or caustic chemicals, vibration; risk of electrocution; extreme heat or cold; and chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, or explosive hazards. The employee may also work in atmospheres that are of an immediate danger to life and health (IDLH).

The noise level in the work environment is usually quiet in the office and moderate to loud while conducting fire inspections and investigations, and loud during certain fireground activities.

Remote work is not available.

Physical Demands

Work requires exerting up to 20 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 10 pounds of force to move objects. Duties require the ability to read, interpret, and analyze detailed information and documents; communicate effectively with others; and receive and respond to verbal and written communication in person, by telephone, and through electronic means.

Additionally, the following physical abilities are required:

  • Balancing: sufficient to maintain body equilibrium to prevent falling while walking, standing or crouching on narrow, slippery, or erratically moving surfaces. The amount of balancing exceeds that needed for ordinary locomotion and maintenance of body equilibrium.
  • Crawling: sufficient to move about on hands and knees or hands and feet.
  • Crouching: sufficient to bend the body downward and forward by bending leg and spine.
  • Feeling: sufficient to perceive attributes of objects, such as size, shape, temperature or texture by touching with skin, particularly that of fingertips.
  • Fingering: sufficient to pick, pinch, type, or otherwise work, primarily with fingers rather than with the whole hand as in handling.
  • Grasping: sufficient to apply pressure to an object with the fingers and palm.
  • Handling: sufficient to pick, hold, or otherwise work, primarily with the whole hand.
  • Hearing: sufficient to perceive the nature of sounds at normal speaking levels with or without correction. Ability to receive detailed information through oral communication, and to make the discrimination in sound.
  • Kneeling: sufficient to bend legs at knee to come to a rest on knee or knees.
  • Lifting: sufficient to raise objects from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position-to-position. Occurs to a considerable degree and requires substantial use of upper extremities and back muscles.
  • Mental Acuity: sufficient to make rational decisions through sound logic and deductive processes.
  • Pulling: sufficient to use upper extremities to exert force in order to draw, haul or tug objects in a sustained motion.
  • Pushing: sufficient to use upper extremities to press against something with steady force in order to thrust forward, downward or outward.
  • Reaching: sufficient to extend hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction.
  • Repetitive Motion: Substantial movements (motions) of the wrist, hands, and/or fingers.
  • Speaking: sufficient to express or exchange ideas by means of the spoken word including the ability to convey detailed or important spoken instructions to other workers accurately and concisely.
  • Standing: Particularly for sustained periods of time.
  • Stooping: sufficient to bend body downward and forward by bending spine at the waist. Occurs to a considerable degree and requires full motion of the lower extremities and back muscles.
  • Talking: sufficient to express or exchange ideas by means of the spoken word including those activities in which they must convey detailed or important spoken instructions to other workers accurately, loudly, or quickly.
  • Visual Acuity: sufficient to observe violations of codes, to effectively operate standard office equipment; ability to read and write reports, correspondence, instructions, drawings, etc.; and to operate motor vehicles and/or heavy equipment, by both day and night.
  • Walking: sufficient to move about on foot to accomplish tasks, particularly for long distances or move from one work site to another.

Equipment & Technology

Uses equipment and technology necessary to perform assigned duties, including computers, mobile devices, office equipment, vehicles, specialized equipment, enterprise software, business applications, communication platforms, and other technologies appropriate to the position. Position-specific equipment and technology may include hearing protection (including earmuffs), safety glasses, steel toed boots, gloves (nitrile, latex, leather), hardhat, knee pads, dust masks, traffic cones, safety vest, and fall-restraint equipment when required.

Employees are expected to effectively utilize equipment, software, and technology applicable to their assigned duties, including emerging technologies approved by the City, in accordance with applicable laws, City policies, procedures, information security standards, and confidentiality requirements.

title: Senior Analyzer Field Technician
description:
If you are a Field Service Technician professional looking to grow your career, Emerson has an exciting opportunity for you in Houston, TX. In this role, you will support customers across the Gulf Coast by providing hands‑on service for our Engineered Solutions for Flow and Quality Measurement, helping ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operations in one of the nation’s leading industrial and energy regions.

Our Engineered Solutions portfolio includes custody transfer/fiscal metering systems, analytical process gas systems, continuous emissions monitoring systems, liquid analysis systems, and sustainability solutions. Lifecycle Services cover digital engagements, annual recurring revenue contracts, upgrades, and “As a Service" business models.

description:
Be part of an amazing story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

The Compensation Analyst provides analytical support to the Compensation team and business groups to ensure alignment between compensation programs and business objectives. The analyst understands business goals to support existing compensation plans, develops predictive analytical models to evaluate the impact of proposed changes, and summarizes market research to inform compensation best practices.

What You Will Do

  • Execute assigned compensation programs accurately and on schedule.
  • Support the implementation and maintenance of compensation programs that meet business needs, including commissions, incentives, salary structure analysis, salary adjustments, and program evaluations.
  • Query and analyze complex datasets to gather information for reporting and decision-making.
  • Provide advanced analytical support to align compensation programs with business and HR strategic objectives, assessing the financial impact of pilots, test-and-learn initiatives, new programs, and policy changes.
  • Audit, assess, and summarize current compensation programs through standard and ad hoc reporting to ensure accuracy, effectiveness, and alignment with business goals.
  • Research and resolve both individual and organizational compensation issues.
  • Identify opportunities to improve existing processes and recommend enhancements to increase efficiency and impact.
  • Serve as a liaison to assigned business groups by answering questions, providing compensation insights, and evaluating programs in response to business partner requests.
  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships, and ensures authentic connections with colleagues, customers, and communities.
  • In addition to the essential duties mentioned above, other duties may be assigned.

Skills You Will Need

Analytical & Quantitative Skills: Strong ability to interpret complex data, perform statistical analysis, and use advanced mathematical concepts to assess compensation structures and business impacts.

Data Management & Reporting: Skilled in querying, manipulating, and analyzing large datasets; advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience with data tools such as Oracle HCM, Pay Factors, Microsoft Access, and VBA.

Compensation & HR Expertise: Understanding of compensation structures, salary analysis, incentive programs, and job evaluation principles; ability to align compensation practices with organizational strategy and market benchmarks.

Financial & Business Acumen: Ability to connect compensation decisions to financial outcomes, assess the impact of pilots and new programs, and support business goals through data-driven recommendations.

Communication & Presentation: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to summarize complex analyses and present insights in a clear, concise, and visually compelling way to influence decision-making.

Process Improvement & Problem Solving: Proactive in identifying process inefficiencies, surfacing issues, and recommending enhancements to improve program accuracy, timeliness, and impact.

Collaboration & Relationship Management: Builds effective partnerships with HR and business leaders; serves as a trusted resource for compensation guidance and insights.

Independence & Initiative: Works independently with minimal supervision in a fast-paced, collaborative environment; demonstrates ownership and accountability for deliverables.

Who You Are

  • Candidates with a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience in a related field are encouraged to apply.
  • Regularly required to sit, talk, hear; use hands/fingers to touch, handle, and feel. Occasionally required to move about the workplace and reach with hands and arms. Requires close vision.
  • Able to work a flexible schedule based on department and company needs.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice
  • Tuition reimbursement

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

title: Associate Systems Engineer
description:
The Associate Systems Engineer is an entry-level engineering role responsible for developing foundational knowledge and practical experience in computer systems, system integration, production processes, and engineering methodologies. This position supports engineering and production activities involving hardware assembly, system configuration, troubleshooting, validation, testing, documentation, and rack-level integration while developing the technical skills necessary to independently support engineering projects.

Working under the guidance of Systems Engineers and Senior Systems Engineers, the Associate Systems Engineer learns and supports Production 1 project workflows, Talon production processes, First Article activities, and established engineering procedures. The role develops hands-on experience with computer hardware, BIOS and firmware, networking fundamentals, system security, rack integration, and troubleshooting methodologies.

The Associate Systems Engineer follows established work instructions and engineering procedures while developing the technical judgment, problem-solving skills, and product knowledge necessary to progress toward independent project execution as a Systems Engineer.

This position typically requires an Associate degree, technical certification, relevant technical training, or equivalent experience. Work is primarily performed under established procedures with guidance from more experienced engineering team members.

Essential functions

  • Technical Development: Develop a working knowledge of computer architectures, system hardware, server components, storage, networking fundamentals, system security, BIOS, firmware, and other technologies used in system integration and production environments.
  • Production Engineering Support: Learn and support Production project workflows and engineering processes. Assist Systems Engineers and Senior Systems Engineers with assigned project activities while developing an understanding of project requirements, engineering deliverables, and production readiness.
  • Hardware Assembly & Configuration: Perform hardware chassis disassembly, component installation, configuration, and reassembly in accordance with established engineering procedures, manufacturer requirements, and Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) practices.
  • System Integration: Support the integration of hardware and software components into complete systems. Assist with system configuration and other integration activities according to established engineering documentation and customer requirements.
  • Rack Integration: Assist with rack-level integration activities, including hardware installation, equipment placement, cable routing and cable management. Develop an understanding of rack infrastructure, networking, power, weight distribution, and serviceability considerations.
  • BIOS & Firmware Management: Develop knowledge of BIOS and firmware configuration and management. Assist with applying, verifying, and documenting approved BIOS, firmware, and hardware configurations according to project requirements.
  • System Validation & Testing: Support engineering teams with system validation and testing activities. Execute established test procedures, document results, identify failures or discrepancies, and escalate issues to the appropriate engineering resource.

Working closely with employees, supervisors, managers, union representatives, and cross-functional partners, the Labor Relations Specialist helps ensure fair and consistent application of workplace policies, effective resolution of employee concerns, and constructive labor-management relationships.


The role serves as a key resource for employee and labor relations matters while supporting a compliant, respectful, and productive work environment

  • Support employee relations and labor relations activities to ensure consistent application of company policies, procedures, and workplace standards.

title: Autopsy Technician (PCN 061993)
description:
Job Description

Join the Department of Health!
We’re thrilled to welcome you!
We’ve made our application process more accessible than ever.
Please take a look at our job announcement below.
If you can see yourself in this role, apply now—your next opportunity awaits!

This position is open to Alaskan Residents only.
Please check out the residency definition to determine if you qualify.


What you will be doing:
As the Autopsy Technician, you will assist the State Medical Examiner Forensic Pathologists with forensic postmortem examinations. Your responsibilities will include conducting a range of activities to assist in determining the cause and manner of death. These activities include, but are not limited to, photography, radiology, the collection of postmortem specimens, fingerprinting, and the collection and preservation of evidence.

Our organization, mission, and culture:
The Division of Public Health's mission is to protect and promote the health of Alaskans. The Division of Public Health exemplifies the values of accountability, respect, human potential, integrity, and scientific excellence.

The benefits of joining our team: This role allows you to be a valuable member of a small, innovative team committed to respect and integrity while connecting with your community. You will also be entitled to health insurance, 12 paid holidays per year, and personal leave. This role will provide you with the opportunity to explore the field of forensics and gain valuable work experience for a career in criminal justice, forensics, and/or law enforcement, all while serving the people of Alaska during the most difficult times. Come, learn, and grow in the Last Frontier while making a difference where we live, work, and play.

The working environment you can expect:
This position is located at 5455 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Ave. in Anchorage. The daily work environment involves standing for long periods of time, frequent lifting, and maneuvering of bodies, exposure to infectious diseases, hazardous substances, and noxious odors. The ability to lift and maneuver up to 300 pounds with mechanical devices is required.

Who we are looking for:
  • Attention to Detail: Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail.

title: Payment Analyst
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Payment Analyst based in France.

Join a newly established Payment Operations team focused on creating end-to-end visibility across a complex payment funnel serving millions of active users.
You’ll investigate payment performance across more than a dozen payment service providers, identifying issues before they become business-critical.
Your analysis will help distinguish technical defects from user-behavior patterns and uncover the bottlenecks with the greatest impact on authorization and conversion.
You’ll turn complex payment and customer data into clear insights that can guide Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Fraud teams.
The role offers significant autonomy, with the opportunity to build diagnostic processes, dashboards, alerts, and reporting capabilities from the ground up.
You’ll work in a fast-moving environment where experimentation, practical problem-solving, and small proof-of-concepts are preferred over lengthy planning cycles.
This is an opportunity to become a trusted expert on payment funnel health while directly contributing to measurable improvements in a rapidly scaling international business.

Accountabilities

  • Take diagnostic ownership of checkout and payment funnel health, proactively identifying alerts, anomalies, insights, and defects before they become business-critical.

  • Lead root-cause investigations into funnel drop-offs and payment declines, distinguishing technical or engineering issues from user-behavior patterns.

  • Analyze authorization rates, decline codes, payment performance, and other funnel metrics to identify the highest-impact bottlenecks and improvement opportunities.

  • Investigate performance across multiple payment service providers and identify differences, outages, or recurring issues requiring attention.

  • Support regular funnel reporting for cross-functional stakeholders, translating payment data into clear insights and recommendations that can improve authorization rates and conversion.

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Fraud teams to investigate payment issues, processor outages, and other funnel-related challenges.

  • Communicate technical and analytical findings clearly to stakeholders who may not have deep payments expertise.

  • Build and improve dashboards, alerts, reporting, and diagnostic processes that increase visibility into payment funnel performance.

  • Develop into a trusted point of contact for payment funnel health, helping establish best practices within the broader team.

  • Work proactively in an evolving environment, creating practical solutions from first principles where established processes or playbooks do not yet exist.

    • Requirements:

    • Hands-on understanding of payment funnels and payment operations, including concepts such as interchange, decline codes, foreign exchange (FX), tokenization, 3DS, and fraud fundamentals.

    • Demonstrated experience performing root-cause analysis on funnel drop-offs, declines, or payment performance issues, including distinguishing technical causes from behavioral patterns.

    • Ability to analyze complex data and customer-behavior insights and communicate findings clearly to audiences without extensive technical or payments expertise.

    • Strong investigative mindset, with the initiative to independently identify and explore issues rather than waiting for predefined tasks.

    • Comfortable working in ambiguous, fast-changing environments where processes and playbooks may still be developing.

    • Nice to have: Familiarity with self-service BI and dashboarding tools to accelerate independent analysis.

    • Nice to have: Strong SQL skills for conducting independent investigations and data analysis.

    • Nice to have: Experience working in a high-growth or rapidly evolving organization.

    • Nice to have: Experience comparing payment performance across multiple PSPs.

    • Strong English communication skills, as English is the primary working language in the international team.

      • Benefits:

      • Competitive salary: €40,000–€60,000 per year, with compensation potentially varying according to experience and seniority.

      • Employee stock options: Opportunity to participate in an employee stock options program.

      • Performance incentives: Access to various bonus programs, including performance-based and referral bonuses.

      • Additional paid leave: Opportunities to earn additional paid time off through applicable bonus programs.

      • Autonomy and ownership: Join a newly formed function where you can help establish processes, tools, and ways of working from the ground up.

title: Clinical Psychologist -- Monterey
description:
Are you a psychologist looking to make a real impact with an underserved population?

This setting may surprise you—in the best way.


It’s late morning.

You’re sitting across from someone most people have stopped really seeing.


They’ve been labeled “non-compliant,” “difficult,” “confused,” or “behavioral.”
Their chart is thick. Their history fragmented. Their life—reduced to diagnoses and risk factors.


But when you slow down, listen carefully, and meet them where they are, something shifts.


They regulate.
They learn to trust.
They remember they are still a person with a story.



And then you realize something important: This work matters more than you were ever told it could.


Why Skilled Nursing? Why Now?


Many psychologists never imagine themselves working in skilled nursing facilities. Not because they wouldn’t be good at it—but because no one ever explained what it actually looks like. And yet, the signs are clear it’s a setting where they are much needed:


With adults 65+ projected to reach 20% of the U.S. population by 2030, demand for clinical psychology and geropsychology in skilled nursing is rapidly increasing. Older nursing home residents have high rates of mental health and cognitive needs, creating a critical need for specialized psychological care in the setting.


At Executive Mental Health (EMH), we focus specifically on this critical and growing need for quality mental healthcare in the skilled nursing facility setting. For 30 years, EMH has offered clinically practical, human-centered work to individuals residing in skilled nursing facilities, who often feel invisible. We serve individuals navigating:


  • Serious mental illness
  • Cognitive decline and neuropsychiatric conditions
  • Medical complexity and disability
  • Trauma, grief, identity loss, and profound transitions


The Role: Psychology Where It Counts


EMH is looking for talented clinicians able to support this population for full-time work in the SNF setting. As a Clinical Psychologist at EMH, you are not working in isolation. You become part of a multi-disciplinary team, collaborating with psychiatrists, neuropsychologists, nursing staff, social services, and facility leadership to stabilize care, reduce suffering, and improve quality of life in real time.


This is psychology that:

  • Prevents hospitalizations
  • Reduces behavioral crises
  • Supports staff under pressure
  • Restores dignity to residents who feel forgotten


What You’ll Be Doing


Working on site at partner SNF facilities near you, your work will be meaningful, varied, and grounded in clinical best practices. You will:


  • Assess, diagnose, and treat individuals in skilled nursing facilities
  • Provide psychological services to geriatric, disabled, and medically complex populations
  • Manage an active caseload with support from your clinical manager and administrative team
  • Collaborate closely with facility staff, offering consultation, guidance, and in-services
  • Complete documentation aligned with medical necessity and Medicare standards.
  • Provide care by meeting residents where they reside, in skilled nursing facilities.


Most importantly, you won’t be working alone: EMH has built systems around our clinicians so you can focus on care.



Requirements

Who This Role Is For


This role is for psychologists who:


  • Hold a PhD or PsyD in Clinical Psychology
  • Are licensed in California
  • Are Medicare-eligible (we assist with credentialing and paneling)
  • Value evidence-based practice and clinical flexibility
  • Are comfortable working with complexity and ambiguity
  • Want autonomy without isolation, and support without micromanagement


You don’t need to have prior experience in skilled nursing facilities to apply. What you need is curiosity, compassion, and the ability to see the person behind the chart.



Benefits

What You’ll Gain


EMH aims to serve as a stable, thoughtful partner during your time with the company, and that includes long-term professional development and employment opportunities.


One indicator of that stability is that, when people join EMH, they like to stick around. For example, members of the EMH Executive Leadership Team have been with the organization for an average of more than nine years; for neuropsychologists, and, more than half of the Clinical Psychologists have been part of the practice for over five years.


We believe that EMH has created an environment in which clinicians establish meaningful, longstanding careers, which, in turn, provides a sense of stability for colleagues, patients, and healthcare partners alike.


Benefits


  • Flexible schedules with true work–life balance
  • Competitive W-2 salary + additional compensation opportunity programs
  • Health insurance: Medical and dental
  • Childcare reimbursement
  • 401(k) matching
  • Vacation and sick pay
  • Referral program
  • Professional development assistance including coverage of license fees and CE costs, plus access to in-house CEs
  • A fully supported home office setup (laptop, printer, IT support)
  • Ongoing clinical consultation with experienced, collaborative colleagues
  • Real opportunities for professional growth in a stable, mission-driven organization


A Final Thought



If you’ve ever felt pulled toward work that is deeper, more human, and more impactful,
If you want to use your training in a way that genuinely changes lives,
If you’re open to discovering a setting that may surprise you,



This may be the place where you can make a real impact.


To apply or learn more, please send your CV (cover letter optional) to careers (at) emhla (dot) com. We look forward to meeting you!

title: Team Leader of Technology
description:
Network Engineering Team Lead

Wilmington, DE

Monday – Friday 8:00 am – 5:00 pm

Remote

The Network Engineering Team Lead (Cloud) leads a team of network engineers responsible for designing, implementing, securing, and maintaining the organization's cloud and hybrid network infrastructure. This role combines hands-on technical leadership with people management, ensuring network reliability, scalability, and security across multi-cloud and on-premises environments while mentoring engineers and driving process improvement.

Some of the things that you’ll be doing:

Team Leadership & Supervision

  • Supervise, mentor, and develop a team of cloud network engineers, including performance management, scheduling, and career development.
  • Assign and prioritize project work, incident response, and on-call rotations.
  • Conduct 1:1s, performance reviews, and support hiring/onboarding of team members.

Cloud Network Architecture & Engineering

  • Design and oversee implementation of secure, scalable network architectures primarily in Azure (VPCs/VNets, subnets, peering, transit gateways, load balancers).
  • Manage hybrid connectivity solutions (VPN, Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, SD-WAN).
  • Own network segmentation, routing, DNS, and firewall policy design in cloud environments.

Operations & Reliability

  • Ensure high availability and performance of cloud network infrastructure; lead incident response and root-cause analysis for network outages.
  • Establish and monitor SLAs/SLOs for network performance and uptime.
  • Drive automation of network provisioning and configuration management.
  • Drive Elastic Observability implementation.

Security & Compliance

  • Partner with security teams to enforce network security best practices (zero trust, micro-segmentation, encryption in transit).
  • Ensure compliance with relevant standards (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI-DSS as applicable).
  • Support audits and vulnerability remediation efforts related to network infrastructure.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with Cloud, DevOps, Security, and application teams to support infrastructure and deployment needs.
  • Serve as an escalation point for complex network issues.
  • Communicate network strategy, risks, and roadmap to IT leadership

What technical skills, qualifications, and experience do you need?

  • 7+ years of experience in network engineering, infrastructure engineering, or a related field, with significant experience designing and supporting enterprise-scale cloud and hybrid network environments.
  • 2+ years of experience leading, supervising, or mentoring network engineering teams, including experience with performance management, work prioritization, and technical development.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Microsoft Azure networking, including VNets, subnets, peering, routing, load balancing, network security groups, Azure Firewall, DNS, and related cloud networking services.
  • Proven experience designing and managing hybrid cloud connectivity, including VPN, ExpressRoute, SD-WAN, and connectivity between cloud and on-premises environments.
  • Strong understanding of core networking concepts and technologies, including TCP/IP, routing, switching, DNS, DHCP, firewalls, network segmentation, VPNs, and load balancing.
  • Experience with network security and zero-trust principles, including segmentation, encryption, firewall policy, identity-based access, and vulnerability remediation.
  • Experience with network automation and infrastructure as code, using tools such as Terraform, Ansible, PowerShell, Python, or similar technologies.
  • Experience with network monitoring and observability, including implementing or supporting tools such as Elastic Observability, Azure Monitor, or comparable platforms.
  • Demonstrated experience leading incident response, troubleshooting complex network issues, performing root-cause analysis, and driving remediation in high-availability environments.
  • Experience working cross-functionally with Cloud, DevOps, Security, and application teams, with the ability to communicate complex technical concepts and risks to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience working in environments subject to security, compliance, and regulatory requirements such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, or PCI-DSS.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Job Title: Elephant Specialist
Department: Wildlife
Reports To: Animal Collections Manager
FLSA Status: Non-exempt

White Oak conserves and sustains some of the earth's rarest wild animals through innovative training, research, education, and conservation breeding programs that contribute to the survival of wildlife in nature. The conservation programs span 600 acres along the St. Mary’s River in northeast Florida, surrounded by 22,000 acres of mixed forest and wetlands that make up the beautiful White Oak property. Founded in 1982, White Oak leads professional efforts to improve veterinary care, develop holistic animal management techniques, and better understand the biology of critically endangered species by providing excellent care and managing conservation programs for over 30 species of imperiled wildlife in large, naturalistic habitats.
White Oak Mission:
Saving endangered wildlife and habitats through sustainable populations, expanding education initiatives, and responsible land stewardship.
Job Summary:
The Elephant Specialist delivers exceptional, safe elephant care to advance White Oak’s elephant conservation programs. This position contributes directly to the White Oak Conservation mission by supporting the elephant husbandry program.
Essential Duties:
o Participates in the daily care of the animals in designated area, to include feeding, cleaning, medicating, training, enrichment, and record keeping activities.
o Participates with hand rearing, animal transfers, introductions, operant conditioning, and area research projects.
o Trains new behaviors with elephants in protected contact system.
o Participates in advanced elephant husbandry practices such as footcare, blood collections, and semen collections.
o Participates with the elephant health team to conduct elephant medical procedures and treatments.
o Notifies supervisor of supplies, tools and equipment needed in the elephant area.
o Performs animal care facilities maintenance to include mowing, weed-eating, pressure washing, dirt and substrate work, gate adjustments, lock lubrication, limb pick up, and other minor repairs.
o Maintains records and reports related to the elephant collection.
o Maintains, cleans, and organizes work and break areas, food storage, food prep, vehicles, and equipment.
o Participates with intern training including animal husbandry and management, record keeping, research, conservation, and education projects.
o Maintains the highest level of safety in the workplace through staff training and implementation of safety protocols and procedures.
o Possesses excellent interpersonal and communication skills necessary to establish and maintain effective working relationships with staff, professional colleagues, and the public, both in person and through phone, e-mail, and written correspondence.
o Handles multiple tasks simultaneously; works in an environment subject to constant interruptions and quickly changing priorities; prioritizes responsibilities and performs effective time-management.
o Operates small equipment and farm machinery, as needed.

description:

As trusted advisors to our customers, providing guidance on migration best practices, risk mitigation, and innovative solutions, you will be responsible for leading the end-to-end migration assessment process, ensuring adherence to AWS well-architected principles, optimizing wave sequencing, and managing risks throughout the programme lifecycle.

title: Supply Chain Officer (P)
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process.

For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates:

  1. Internal candidates
  2. Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories: Bahamas, Barbados, Cabo Verde, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu

Second tier candidates include:
All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM.

Organizational Context and Scope

Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission and direct supervision of the Head of Resources Management (HoRM), and in close collaboration with the Regional Office in Cairo and in coordination with the Supply Chain Division at Headquarters (HQ), the Supply Chain Officer will be responsible and accountable for overseeing the supply chain activities, guided by Supply Chain Management (SCM) objectives to deliver quality goods/services to the beneficiaries at optimal price and in a timely manner.

1. Conduct strategic planning for supply chain-related activities of the Country Office (CO) in close collaboration with internal and external stakeholders in the country, as well as relevant units at HQ.

2. Conduct logistics capacity assessments and market research to keep abreast decision-makers about local market trends and developments; analyze statistical data and market reports on the commodity situation, production patterns, and availability of goods and services.

3. Supervise, manage and provide first-line support and guidance for all SCM-related tasks and activities, including planning, budgeting, scheduling and provision of goods and services needed by the CO. Prepare regular progress reports, statistical information and briefing notes, as required.

4. Lead and supervise the supply chain activities in the CO, including planning, procurement, warehouse management, transport and distribution, fleet, assets and facilities management, logistics information management and reporting, and provide guidance and training to the relevant staff with respect to the related policies, rules and regulations.

5. Identify supply chain bottlenecks (value stream mapping) and optimize the processes to fill the gaps and ensure beneficiaries receive quality goods and services in a timely and efficient manner.

6. Review procurement requests, identify service providers, and evaluate information regarding vendors’ performance in terms of quality, prices, and timely delivery of goods/services. Maintain a pool of qualified vendors.

7. Solicit bids, quotations, and tender documents, oversee the bidding process and provide guidance for executing the procurement transactions, analyze the offers assuring conformity to specified requirements; conduct appraisals and select suppliers, and confirm terms of payment; supervise the preparation and processing of the purchase orders, and ensure receiving authorization in line with the CO’s Delegation of Authority (DoA) matrix.

8. Liaise with the programme management and provide first-line technical support in the preparation and issuance of “Call for Proposals” and bidding documents for the tendering processes of the programmes/projects. Ensure that bidding processes are conducted fairly, transparently and in accordance with the existing procurement rules and regulations.

9. In coordination with relevant parties, ensure timely submission of asset procurement and other reports within the CO, Regional Office (RO) and relevant HQ departments, as appropriate.

10. Establish and manage appropriate and robust internal control mechanisms for the SCM process to safeguard the Organization's assets and prevent fraud, while ensuring that country-specific

11. administrative procedures are in place and followed in accordance with the Organization's rules and regulations.


12. Monitor the maintenance and repair of office facilities, including preventive maintenance. Establish maintenance agreements with competent service providers, when it is feasible and determined to be cost-effective.

13. Supervise, train, and guide the SCM staff of CO, while monitoring, evaluating, and promoting their professional and career development.

14. Represent the CO in the United Nations (UN) inter-agency meetings and forums related to supply chain management. Collaborate on sharing resources to achieve common goals and implementation of UN global initiatives.

15. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Master’s degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Procurement, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or
  • University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Experience in managing diverse procurement and logistics operations;
  • Demonstrated experience in training and managing large teams of co-workers, managing vendors and suppliers;
  • Experience in managing diverse procurement and logistics operations;
  • Experience in managing supply chain operations in complex emergencies, fragile and/or hardship duty stations, including supporting humanitarian operations under challenging security and operational conditions; and,
  • Demonstrated experience in planning and implementing procurement, warehousing,
    fleet, and logistics activities in volatile environments while ensuring business continuity and compliance with organizational policies and donor requirements.

Skills

  • Extensive knowledge of IOM/UN internal procurement and financial rules, as well as IOM's systems and processes as they apply to procurement and logistics; and,
  • Excellent level of computer literacy and good knowledge of Oracle is an advantage.

Languages

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Arabic is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.
  • Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.
  • Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.
  • Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction.
  • Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings.

Notes

Internationally recruited professional staff are required to be mobile. Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to all clearances, including medical and security as well as accreditation, any residency or visa requirements. Vacancies close at 23:59 local time Geneva, Switzerland on the respective closing date. No late applications will be accepted.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, harassment, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and any forms of discrimination. IOM is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children.

IOM conducts reference checks and background verification, including through system wide databases such as ClearCheck, to help ensure that candidates have no record of misconduct, including on sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, or fraud. Candidates are expected to uphold these standards and principles at all times.

IOM does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process—whether for application, interview, processing, training, or otherwise—and does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM WAVE system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Payment Analyst
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Payment Analyst based in Spain.

Join a newly established Payment Operations team focused on creating end-to-end visibility across a complex payment funnel serving millions of active users.
You’ll investigate payment performance across more than a dozen payment service providers, identifying issues before they become business-critical.
Your analysis will help distinguish technical defects from user-behavior patterns and uncover the bottlenecks with the greatest impact on authorization and conversion.
You’ll turn complex payment and customer data into clear insights that can guide Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Fraud teams.
The role offers significant autonomy, with the opportunity to build diagnostic processes, dashboards, alerts, and reporting capabilities from the ground up.
You’ll work in a fast-moving environment where experimentation, practical problem-solving, and small proof-of-concepts are preferred over lengthy planning cycles.
This is an opportunity to become a trusted expert on payment funnel health while directly contributing to measurable improvements in a rapidly scaling international business.

Accountabilities

  • Take diagnostic ownership of checkout and payment funnel health, proactively identifying alerts, anomalies, insights, and defects before they become business-critical.

  • Lead root-cause investigations into funnel drop-offs and payment declines, distinguishing technical or engineering issues from user-behavior patterns.

  • Analyze authorization rates, decline codes, payment performance, and other funnel metrics to identify the highest-impact bottlenecks and improvement opportunities.

  • Investigate performance across multiple payment service providers and identify differences, outages, or recurring issues requiring attention.

  • Support regular funnel reporting for cross-functional stakeholders, translating payment data into clear insights and recommendations that can improve authorization rates and conversion.

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Fraud teams to investigate payment issues, processor outages, and other funnel-related challenges.

  • Communicate technical and analytical findings clearly to stakeholders who may not have deep payments expertise.

  • Build and improve dashboards, alerts, reporting, and diagnostic processes that increase visibility into payment funnel performance.

  • Develop into a trusted point of contact for payment funnel health, helping establish best practices within the broader team.

  • Work proactively in an evolving environment, creating practical solutions from first principles where established processes or playbooks do not yet exist.

    • Requirements:

    • Hands-on understanding of payment funnels and payment operations, including concepts such as interchange, decline codes, foreign exchange (FX), tokenization, 3DS, and fraud fundamentals.

    • Demonstrated experience performing root-cause analysis on funnel drop-offs, declines, or payment performance issues, including distinguishing technical causes from behavioral patterns.

    • Ability to analyze complex data and customer-behavior insights and communicate findings clearly to audiences without extensive technical or payments expertise.

    • Strong investigative mindset, with the initiative to independently identify and explore issues rather than waiting for predefined tasks.

    • Comfortable working in ambiguous, fast-changing environments where processes and playbooks may still be developing.

    • Nice to have: Familiarity with self-service BI and dashboarding tools to accelerate independent analysis.

    • Nice to have: Strong SQL skills for conducting independent investigations and data analysis.

    • Nice to have: Experience working in a high-growth or rapidly evolving organization.

    • Nice to have: Experience comparing payment performance across multiple PSPs.

    • Strong English communication skills, as English is the primary working language in the international team.

      • Benefits:

      • Competitive salary: €40,000–€60,000 per year, with compensation potentially varying according to experience and seniority.

      • Employee stock options: Opportunity to participate in an employee stock options program.

      • Performance incentives: Access to various bonus programs, including performance-based and referral bonuses.

      • Additional paid leave: Opportunities to earn additional paid time off through applicable bonus programs.

      • Learning budget: Personal budget dedicated to professional development and learning.

      • Paid volunteering: Opportunities to participate in volunteering activities during paid working time.

      • Flexible work location: Choose between office-based and remote work, with opportunities to combine work and travel.

      • International environment: Work in a global team where English is the primary business language.

      • Career development: Strong opportunities for personal and professional growth supported by structured feedback and promotion processes.

      • High-impact role: Help scale a fast-growing international marketplace while directly contributing to payment performance, customer conversion, and business growth.

      • Autonomy and ownership: Join a newly formed function where you can help establish processes, tools, and ways of working from the ground up.

title: Retail Lead
description:
Job Summary


Who We Are

Bargain Lane is a fast-growing local discount retail, online auction, and bargain bin store built on one simple idea: unbeatable deals, every single day. With stores across Indiana and Michigan, bargain bins where diggers are rewarded, and online auctions where hunters bid and win from anywhere, our inventory is always moving, always changing, and always a treasure hunt. We don't do polished—we do real. We are fast-moving, hands-on, and built for people who love the grind of making something work.

What We’re Building

Bargain Lane Live is our live-stream selling operation powered by Whatnot, anchored directly out of our retail locations. We are combining brick-and-mortar retail management with real-time live auction sales.

The Role

We are looking for a high-energy hybrid leader who can seamlessly bridge our physical sales floor and our digital live channel. As a Retail Lead & Live WhatNot Show Host, you will spend part of your shift running floor operations—opening/closing the store, managing cash, supervising staff, and supporting customers—and part of your shift locked on camera holding down our live auction window.

This is live selling, closer to QVC and live auctioneering than influencer content. You will be paired with a behind-the-scenes show assistant while on camera, maintaining a relentless pace across 250+ items while driving real-time sales numbers.



Key Responsibilities & Essential Functions


1. Live WhatNot Host & On-Camera Sales (Show Shift Focus)

  • High-Pace Hosting: Command the camera during live auction windows (typically scheduled within 4:00 PM – 8:00 PM blocks), pacing through 250+ items with non-stop energy.
  • Closing & Conversions: Drive live bids through fast-paced product descriptions, call-to-actions, and continuous engagement.
  • Audience & Chat Engagement: Address viewers by name, build chat momentum, pivot selling styles in real-time based on live audience signals, and celebrate winning bids.
  • Post-Show Debriefs: Participate in daily debriefs to evaluate sales data, viewer retention, and product performance to continuously optimize future shows.

2. Retail Operations & Leadership (Store Shift Focus)

  • Opening & Closing Procedures: Execute daily store opening and closing protocols, including security checks, register setup, and store lockdown.
  • Team Supervision: Assist in directing, delegating tasks to, and training retail team members on floor standards, customer service, and loss prevention.
  • Cash Handling & Register Audits: Reconcile cash drawers, conduct register audits, manage transactions, and resolve drawer discrepancies.
  • Floor Management & Customer Service: Assist in-store customers with product inquiries, sales, and returns, ensuring an engaging, organized store environment.

3. Inventory & Security Compliance

  • Merchandise Stocking: Maintain organized floor displays, monitor bin stock levels, and prep featured merchandise for live streams.
  • Loss Prevention: Enforce security policies and loss prevention strategies to safeguard store inventory.
  • Company Compliance: Uphold all company policies, procedures, and operational standards across both physical retail and live streaming workflows.

The Job You Will Perform:

  • Working within the Reliability Team of International Paper’s Technology Group, the Electrical Power Distribution SME serves as a corporate technical expert responsible for ensuring maximum uptime, safety, and reliability of our complex electrical infrastructure. This role bridges field operations, maintenance execution, and engineering to mitigate operational risks and optimize power distribution performance.
  • Key Responsibilities
    • Technical Authority & Oversight: Act as the lead technical resource for LV/MV switchgear, transformers, turbine generator controls, backup generators, UPS battery systems, and protective relaying.
    • Maintenance & Procedures: Plan, author, and approve safety and operating procedures for high-risk electrical troubleshooting, repair, and retrofit activities.
    • Safety & Compliance: Enforce strict adherence to internal & external electrical safety programs, National Electrical Testing Association (NETA) standards, National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards, and local/national/global electrical codes.
    • Root-Cause Analysis: Lead forensic investigations and root-cause analysis (RCA) for any electrical anomalies, equipment failures, or system trips that exceed facility capabilities.
    • Project & Quality Oversight: Provide Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QAQC) for ongoing electrical construction, capacity upgrades, and component modifications.
    • Training & Mentorship: Train critical facility engineers / champions, technicians, and cross-functional teams on equipment operations, system changes, and best practices.

  • Support EPD asset-management efforts by analyzing reliability, maintenance and operating data, conducting field assessments and recommending improvements that prevent failures and reduce maintenance costs.

  • Support effective execution of the Reliability System elements, with an emphasis on those that impact the care, operation, and precision repair of electrical power distribution equipment.

  • Support planned and unplanned outages through on-site and remote technical assistance.

  • Apply reliability life-cycle knowledge and engineering standards to capital projects, including specifications, Capital Investment Proposals, necessary factory acceptance testing, installation quality and commissioning.

  • Partner with Global Sourcing to support value-added supplier contracts and maintain quality standards for electrical power distribution equipment.

  • Deliver hands-on technical training and transfer knowledge through one-on-one, small-group, classroom and field instruction.

  • Develop and validate reliability standards and best practices, build technical networks across manufacturing locations and mentor facility champions.

  • Ability to respond to manufacturing facilities on short notice.

The Qualifications, Skills and Knowledge You Will Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or a similar engineering discipline is preferred, industry experience will be considered.

  • Industry certification in EPD technology, maintenance, or reliability is preferred. Candidates without certification must obtain it within their first year.

  • 5-15 years of combined maintenance and technical experience in EPD & Turbine Generator equipment and operations; pulp and paper industry experience is preferred.

  • Thorough knowledge of EPD equipment design, construction and operation.

  • Working knowledge of reliability systems, root cause failure analysis, predictive maintenance techniques and computerized maintenance management systems such as SAP-PM is preferred.

  • Demonstrated leadership and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively with team members at all levels of the organization.

  • Excellent written, verbal, consulting and technical-training skills, including the ability to teach in classroom and field settings.

  • Ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally (by exception) up to 75% of the time and provide support to manufacturing facilities, as needed.

title: Director of Neuropsychology
description:
Director of Neuropsychology

Build and lead the future of Neuropsychology at CBC.

Cognitive & Behavioral Consultants (CBC) is seeking a Director of Neuropsychology to lead and grow our Neuropsychology program. Following the departure of our former Director, we are looking for a motivated and entrepreneurial neuropsychologist who is excited by the opportunity to take an established service area and help shape its next chapter.

This is a unique opportunity for a clinician who has been licensed and practicing in neuropsychology for at least two years, particularly with children and adolescents, and is ready to take the next step into leadership.

As Director, you will have the opportunity to help build the future of Neuropsychology at CBC. You will have a meaningful voice in shaping the program, developing clinical services, mentoring clinicians and trainees, strengthening referral relationships, and identifying new opportunities for growth.

You will also be joining a broader behavioral health organization with a strong reputation for evidence-based care and the opportunity to work alongside internationally recognized psychologists and CBT and DBT leaders, including CBC founders Dr. Alec Miller and Dr. Lata McGinn.

About the Opportunity

The Director of Neuropsychology will:

  • Lead and develop CBC's Neuropsychology program
  • Provide comprehensive neuropsychological and psychoeducational evaluations for children, adolescents, and young adults
  • Establish and strengthen clinical standards and assessment practices
  • Mentor, supervise, and support neuropsychologists and trainees
  • Build relationships with schools, physicians, therapists, and other referral partners
  • Identify opportunities to expand and strengthen Neuropsychology services
  • Collaborate with CBC's clinical leadership and broader behavioral health team
  • Participate in training, consultation, and professional development
  • Help shape the vision, culture, and future growth of the program

Who We're Looking For

We are looking for a licensed psychologist with at least two years of experience practicing in neuropsychology, with a strong background working with children and adolescents and a genuine interest in leadership and program development.

The ideal candidate is:

  • Clinically strong and confident in neuropsychological assessment
  • Passionate about working with children, adolescents, and families
  • Collaborative, thoughtful, and committed to evidence-based care
  • Excited by the opportunity to build and grow something
  • Interested in mentoring and developing other clinicians
  • Comfortable taking initiative and helping shape clinical programs
  • Ready to move from primarily providing clinical care into a broader leadership role

This is more than a Director position. It is an opportunity to build something of your own within an established and growing behavioral health organization.

If you are an experienced neuropsychologist who has been thinking about taking the next step in your career, expanding your leadership experience, and having a meaningful impact on the future of neuropsychology, we would love to hear from you.
