title: Delivery Consultant - Migrations, AWS Professional Services
description:
The Amazon Web Services Professional Services (ProServe) team is seeking a skilled Delivery Consultant to join our team at Amazon Web Services (AWS). In this role, you'll work closely with customers to design, implement, and manage AWS solutions that meet their technical requirements and business objectives. You'll be a key player in driving customer success through their cloud journey, providing technical expertise and best practices throughout the project lifecycle.

Possessing a deep understanding of AWS products and services, as a Delivery Consultant you will be proficient in leading large-scale portfolio assessment and application disposition for enterprise data centre exit programmes spanning multiple countries and regulatory jurisdictions. You'll work closely with stakeholders to gather requirements, assess current infrastructure through discovery tooling and application owner interviews, and propose effective migration strategies to AWS — assigning R-strategies (Rehost, Replatform, Refactor, Retire, Retain, Relocate) and designing wave plans that respect dependency groupings, capacity constraints, and regulatory frozen zones. As trusted advisors to our customers, providing guidance on migration best practices, risk mitigation, and innovative solutions, you will be responsible for leading the end-to-end migration assessment process, ensuring adherence to AWS well-architected principles, optimizing wave sequencing, and managing risks throughout the programme lifecycle.

The AWS Professional Services organization is a global team of experts that help customers realize their desired business outcomes when using the AWS Cloud. We work together with customer teams and the AWS Partner Network (APN) to execute enterprise cloud computing initiatives. Our team provides assistance through a collection of offerings which help customers achieve specific outcomes related to enterprise cloud adoption. We also deliver focused guidance through our global specialty practices, which cover a variety of solutions, technologies, and industries.

Key job responsibilities
• Own Portfolio Assessment for assigned application estates (1,000+ servers), scoring apps across dimensions from Technical Designs and CMDB data
• Apply the migration decision tree to assign R-strategies (Rehost/Replatform/Refactor/Retire/Retain/Relocate) and document rationale in Architecture Decision Records
• Build and maintain dependency maps using applications, resolving conflicting data between tooling output and application owner interviews
• Design wave plans: group applications by dependency, balance capacity, respect regulatory frozen zones, and coordinate across geographies
• Run Tech Bridge sessions with customer application owners to validate disposition decisions and unblock migration paths
• Feed wave planning into AWS Transform, ensuring move groups are sized, sequenced, and ready for factory execution
• Proactively identify and escalate risks to wave timelines — then propose and drive mitigations before they become blockers
• Collaborate with Security, Networking, and Replatform teams to ensure cross-cutting dependencies are addressed in wave sequencing

About the team
Diverse Experiences: AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job below, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS? Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture - Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth - We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance - We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

The position may require up to 50% travel to customer sites.

title: Care Access Specialist I
description:
Join a team that’s transforming mental healthcare. Founded by psychiatrists, Headlight is more than a company: it’s a movement. A movement that exists on the front lines of the mental health crisis, transforming the way people access care and the way clinicians deliver it. In order to help people in their time of need and ensure that every person who comes to us has options, we are transparent about our capabilities, treatments, and coverage, we champion innovation, and we leverage our rich data to continuously implement better ways of delivering care. Our mission is simple but powerful: Improving lives, one session at a time.

Our highly skilled and principled clinical team enjoys autonomy and institutional support so they can put their focus where it should be: on improving patient outcomes. Our clinicians want to do more than help individual clients, so they work to affect the system as a whole, elevating standards of care so that their efforts reverberate far beyond what they could do in private practice.

As the most trusted behavioral health partner in the Western U.S., we’ve established deep relationships that give us unparalleled access, interoperability, and first-priority referrals. This exclusivity, combined with our best-in-class coordinated care and feedback loops, results in superior outcomes and cost savings.

Our services are convenient, accessible, and expert, combining personalized client engagement with advanced technology to enhance, not replace, human connection. Indeed, we hold that human-to-human relationships are indispensable, so from the match to the session to the time between sessions, we provide whole person care so nobody falls through the cracks and there is a brighter path forward for all.

Position Summary

The Care Access Specialist I serves in a critical role as the first person a patient connects with when seeking care at Headlight Health. In this role, the Specialist helps patients feel welcomed, heard, and supported as they begin their care journey.
Care Access Specialists are non-clinical role. Care Access Specialist facilitate access to care, provide peer informed support within the scope of their training, and follow established escalation protocols. Care Access Specialist do not diagnose, independently assess clinical acuity, provide treatment recommendations, deliver psychotherapy, or replace the judgment of licensed clinical professionals.
The Care Access Specialist I provides clear, compassionate guidance about Headlight Health’s services, responds to patient questions, confirms service eligibility, and coordinates appropriate clinician matching. Through empathy, patience, and persistence, the Specialist supports patients through scheduling, onboarding documentation, and related administrative steps to promote a smooth, reassuring transition into care.
This role is a hybrid role that requires 3 days a week in our Downtown Salt Lake City office (136 S Main Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84101). Work hours will be Monday- Friday, 10:30am-7pm MT.

Our Pillars

  • Make things easier.
  • Forge genuine connections.
  • Elevate the standard.

Roles & Responsibilities

Own the Outcome

  • Take accountability for connecting each person to care. Success is a kept first appointment, not simply a scheduled appointment
  • Close the loop on every opportunity by proactively following up and re-engaging people who have not yet started care
  • Respond to new opportunities quickly, with a standard of first outreach within five minutes
Engage and Guide
  • Meet people where they are in their care journey and provide the right combination of information, reassurance, guidance, and encouragement to help them move forward
  • Build supportive, engaging relationships with people who reach out directly or are referred by a healthcare provider, introducing them to Headlight Health’s mental healthcare services
  • Create a positive and reassuring experience for people taking the step of seeking mental health support 1
  • Facilitate access to client care with the appropriate Headlight clinician based on client specific needs; schedule appointment needs, gather accurate information, and determine the appropriate next steps
  • Keep people informed and comfortable throughout the process, addressing questions, concerns, and barriers as they arise
Facilitate the Onboarding Lifecycle
  • Own the onboarding process from first contact through the first kept clinical appointment, including scheduling and collection of required intake paperwork, insurance information, and payment method
  • Follow Headlight’s Service Offer Standard and all applicable guidelines when discussing or introducing additional services
Keep the System Clean
  • Accurately document and maintain client information, interactions, outreach activity, and appointment records
  • Partner with clinicians, operations, and other teams to remove barriers, streamline access to care, and improve the client’s experience
  • Follow all organizational policies, procedures, and legal and regulatory requirements while maintaining a high standard of care
Performance Expectations/Metrics
  • Performance is measured through both activity discipline and the outcomes those activities produce.
  • Activities per day: 100 to 125 (calls, texts, emails)
  • New intakes scheduled: 40 per week
  • Speed to first contact: Within 5 minutes on new incoming opportunities
  • New intakes kept: 30 per week (75% kept rate)

Qualifications

  • • High School Diploma, GED or equivalent required
  • Associate degree, or some college coursework, preferred
  • One (1) year experience in customer service call center environment or similar client-facing role, required
  • Experience in healthcare, behavioral health or client engagement, preferred
  • Strong customer service skills with the ability to build trust and rapport with prospective clients
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including active listening and clear explanation of services
  • Exhibits sound judgment, knowing when to proceed, escalate, clarify or involve other team members, as needed
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple intake tasks, appointments, and follow-ups
  • High attention to detail when entering client information, insurance details, payment information, and documentation
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive health information with professionalism and discretion
  • Basic understanding of healthcare, behavioral health, or outpatient service workflows.
  • Experience using electronic health records, scheduling systems, phone systems, and other digital tools
  • Ability to work collaboratively with clinicians, operations teams, and other departments to support a positive client experience
  • Demonstrated empathy, patience, and professionalism when assisting individuals seeking mental health services

Benefits

  • W2 role with competitive hourly rate and an additional incentive-based pay structure

  • Medical, Dental and Vision on the first of the month after employment (based on FT hours)

  • Paid Vacation, Sick, and Holiday time

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) provides confidential counseling services, resources, and support to help you navigate personal or professional challenges.

  • 401(k) plan with company contribution

  • Hybrid work schedule

  • Opportunity to work in a cutting-edge healthcare technology environment

  • Professional development opportunities and training

  • Collaborative and supportive work culture

  • Impactful role contributing to the enhancement of patient care and healthcare processes

What To Expect

  • Lead, coach, and support Asset Protection colleagues in theft prevention, investigations, apprehension procedures, and company standards.
  • Partner with store leadership to support a safe, secure, and customer-focused environment.
  • Use surveillance, alarm, reporting, and computer systems to monitor activity, document incidents, and support investigations.
  • Respond to customer and colleague incidents, including first aid situations, safety concerns, and potential liability matters.
  • Support store and company policies related to apprehensions, searches, seizures, evidence preservation, and legal compliance.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Lead and develop Asset Protection colleagues by training, coaching, and reinforcing best practices for theft prevention, investigations, and apprehensions.
  • Help reduce loss by supporting programs and routines that prevent theft, fraud, and policy violations involving customers or colleagues.
  • Protect company assets by recovering merchandise, responding to incidents, and apprehending shoplifters or individuals involved in criminal activity.
  • Investigate incidents involving customers, colleagues, or company property, while following company policies and legal requirements.
  • Create clear, timely, and accurate reports for theft incidents, merchandise recoveries, accident investigations, audits, and other assigned activities.
  • Support store compliance by conducting and overseeing audits, identifying gaps, and helping ensure standards are consistently maintained.
  • Build strong partnerships with store leadership and local law enforcement to support investigations and potential criminal cases.
  • Represent the company professionally in court, when needed, for criminal or civil cases involving company interests.
  • Support special assignments, investigations, surveillance, and alarm response as directed by the Store Asset Protection Manager.
  • Create a respectful and inclusive environment that strengthens trust with colleagues, customers, and the communities we serve.

Skills That Matter

Must Have

  • Experience training, coaching, or supervising others in a retail, security, asset protection, or related environment.

  • Ability to identify, investigate, and respond to theft, fraud, safety, and policy-related incidents.

  • Knowledge of or ability to learn company policies and legal requirements related to apprehensions, searches, seizures, and evidence preservation.

  • Ability to complete required security training and maintain certifications required by law.

  • Ability to apprehend shoplifters and respond appropriately to incidents in a retail environment.

  • Maintain regular, dependable attendance and punctuality, and perform other duties as needed.

  • For jobs in New York, a current New York State Security Guard License is required.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with surveillance, alarm, reporting, or case management systems.

  • Experience partnering with local law enforcement or supporting criminal investigations.

  • Strong written communication skills for preparing clear, complete, and timely incident reports.

  • Ability to remain calm, professional, and customer-focused in sensitive or high-pressure situations.

  • Ability to sustain long periods of time in surveillance areas, stand or walk for prolonged periods, and occasionally reach above eye level, stoop, kneel, or crouch.

Physical Activities You Will Perform

  • This role involves performing essential job functions such as communication, collaboration, and use of office and computer systems. Responsibilities include the ability to access and review written and electronic information, and to move within the work environment and interact with workplace materials as needed to carry out job responsibilities.
  • Position requires prolonged periods of standing/walking around store or department.
  • May occasionally involve reaching above eye level, stooping, kneeling, or crouching.
  • Must be able to apprehend shoplifters.
  • Ability to sustain long periods of time enclosed in surveillance areas.
  • Frequently lift/move up to 30lbs.
  • Requires close vision, color vision, and ability to adjust focus.
